literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在1012名因急性呼吸道感染住院的婴儿中,呼吸道合胞病毒下呼吸道疾病住院的疫苗保护效力为77.8%(95%置信区间,66.4%-85.3%),总体情况如下:3个月或更小婴儿为80.2%(95%置信区间,71.1%-86.5%)、2个月或更小婴儿为86.3%(95%置信区间,79.0%-91.1%)、年龄大于2个月至4个月的婴儿为68.2%(95%置信区间,42.2%-82.5%)。 [10.1001/jamapediatrics.2026.3391]
与未感染的对照相比,RSV 感染引起 EMV 水平呈时间依赖性增加,其中含有增加的 RSV-NP 和病毒 RNA 的 EMV 在感染后 72 小时达到峰值。 [10.1007/s00430-026-00886-y]
完成 3 天类固醇治疗后 3 天进行的血培养显示出酵母样生物,后来证实为 Papiliotrema laurentii。抗真菌敏感性测试显示出与普通酵母不同的特征。患者在 6 个月的随访中完全康复并保持无复发。 [10.1620/tjem.2026.j080]

在37°C下,Δ1238、C1238S/Y1246K和Y1246K的复制被延迟,峰值滴度分别比野生型HMPV低约80倍、200倍和25倍。C1238S对照对温度不敏感(T_SH > 40°C),而Y1246K和Δ1238(T_SH = 39°C)和C1238S/Y1246K(T_SH = 38°C)表现出温度敏感表型。C1238S/Y1246K 和 Δ1238 候选物在仓鼠中的复制受到限制,但具有免疫原性并能抵抗 HMPV 攻击。 [10.1128/jvi.00692-26]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Among 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) overall, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) for infants aged 3 months or younger, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) for infants aged 2 months or younger, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) for infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. [10.1001/jamapediatrics.2026.3391]

RSV infection induced a time-dependent increase in EMV levels compared to uninfected controls, with EMVs containing increasing RSV-NP and viral RNA peaking at 72 hours post-infection. [10.1007/s00430-026-00886-y]

In the second quarter of 2025, RSV mortality among children under 5 years reached 60 per 100,000, a 43% increase compared with the same period in 2024. Mortality for the combined group of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus doubled from 20 to 40 per 100,000 in the same age group. [10.64898/2026.08.15.26360470]
Among 179 households with 542 contacts, secondary infection was detected in 110 households (61.5%) and 218 contacts (40.2%); 46.3% were symptomatic. [10.1016/j.jinf.2026.106834]

Blood cultures performed 3 days after completion of 3-day steroid therapy revealed yeast-like organisms, later confirmed as Papiliotrema laurentii. Antifungal susceptibility testing showed a profile distinct from common yeasts. The patient achieved complete resolution and remained relapse-free at 6-month follow-up. [10.1620/tjem.2026.j080]

news.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是五岁以下儿童急性下呼吸道感染的主要原因,对全世界儿童健康构成持续威胁。婴儿早期感染 RSV 会显着增加患儿童哮喘的风险,尤其是有过敏或哮喘家族史的儿童。RSV 还会导致老年人出现严重后果和心脏并发症。 [news-efe9dd69a02d9428]
英国健康安全局 (UKHSA) 报告称,2024 年 9 月启动的国家孕产妇 RSV 疫苗接种 计划在第一年全年就将 6 个月以下婴儿的重症监护入院人数减少了约 50%。 [news-dce26469420652d5]
英国健康安全局 (UKHSA) 报告称,与上一年相比,2025/2026 年冬季冬季 RSV 胸部感染婴儿入住 ICU 和 HDU 的人数减少了 50%。这一减少归因于孕产妇 RSV 疫苗接种 计划。 [news-a00f07dd7e150764]

papers.title: The New Era of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Protection for Infants: A Mini Review of Current Tools for Immunoprophylaxis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aim This mini review describes the history of infant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis and the latest advances in this area. It also reviews the efficacy, safety and impact of the recently introduced prophylactic strategies. Method This narrative review is based on a targeted review of published literature, with emphasis on pivotal clinical trials, regulatory documents and recent real‐world evidence. Results Three immunisation products for preventing RSV in infants have been approved since 2022. These are two long‐acting monoclonal antibodies, nirsevimab and clesrovimab, and a maternal RSV vaccine. The efficacy of these interventions has ranged from 49% to 76% against medically attended RSV‐associated lower respiratory tract infections and from 55% to 91% against hospitalisation due to RSV‐associated lower respiratory tract infection. The efficacy varied between the products and the duration of the follow‐up. Similar or higher effectiveness has been reported in post‐licensure, real‐world evidence studies. Overall, these interventions have been well tolerated, with favourable safety profiles. Conclusion The newly introduced long‐acting monoclonal antibodies and the maternal RSV vaccine have proved highly effective and have demonstrated reassuring safety. They have already been implemented in a number of countries and have substantially reduced the RSV burden in infants.

papers.title_original: The New Era of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Protection for Infants: A Mini Review of Current Tools for Immunoprophylaxis

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; Orthopneumovirus hominis, including RSV-A and RSV-B) immunoprophylaxis for infants, focusing on the central question of the efficacy, safety, and impact of recently introduced prophylactic strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes published literature with emphasis on pivotal clinical trials, regulatory documents, and recent real-world evidence; eligibility criteria and selection methods are not explicitly reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Three immunoprophylaxis products for infants have been approved since 2022: two long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab and clesrovimab) and a maternal RSV vaccine, with efficacy ranging from 49% to 76% against medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections and 55% to 91% against hospitalization due to RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report heterogeneity in efficacy estimates by geographic region, socioeconomic status, or high-risk subgroups, nor does it address long-term safety beyond initial approval phases.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Post-licensure effectiveness studies should prioritize monitoring durability of protection, safety in preterm infants, and implementation strategies in low-resource settings to optimize global RSV burden reduction.

analysis.summary_en: This mini-review evaluates recent advances in infant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis, focusing on two long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab and clesrovimab) and a maternal RSV vaccine approved since 2022. Across pivotal trials and real-world evidence, efficacy against medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections ranges from 49% to 76%, and against hospitalization from 55% to 91%, with favorable safety profiles. These interventions have been implemented in multiple countries and have substantially reduced infant RSV burden. Key gaps include limited data on long-term safety, durability of protection, and effectiveness across diverse populations and settings.

elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Three immunoprophylaxis products for infants have been approved since 2022: two long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab and clesrovimab) and a maternal RSV vaccine, with efficacy ranging from 49% to 76% against medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections and 55% to 91% against hospitalization due to RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection.

papers.title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 婴儿保护的新时代:当前免疫预防工具的简要回顾
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Aim This mini review describes the history of infant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis and the latest advances in this area. It also reviews the efficacy, safety and impact of the recently introduced prophylactic strategies. Method This narrative review is based on a targeted review of published literature, with emphasis on pivotal clinical trials, regulatory documents and recent real‐world evidence. Results Three immunisation products for preventing RSV in infants have been approved since 2022. These are two long‐acting monoclonal antibodies, nirsevimab and clesrovimab, and a maternal RSV vaccine. The efficacy of these interventions has ranged from 49% to 76% against medically attended RSV‐associated lower respiratory tract infections and from 55% to 91% against hospitalisation due to RSV‐associated lower respiratory tract infection. The efficacy varied between the products and the duration of the follow‐up. Similar or higher effectiveness has been reported in post‐licensure, real‐world evidence studies. Overall, these interventions have been well tolerated, with favourable safety profiles. Conclusion The newly introduced long‐acting monoclonal antibodies and the maternal RSV vaccine have proved highly effective and have demonstrated reassuring safety. They have already been implemented in a number of countries and have substantially reduced the RSV burden in infants.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 这篇简短的综述介绍了婴儿 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 免疫预防的历史以及该领域的最新进展。它还回顾了最近引入的预防策略的有效性、安全性和影响。方法 本叙述性综述基于对已发表文献的有针对性的综述,重点是关键临床试验、监管文件和最新的现实世界证据。结果 自 2022 年以来,已有三种用于预防婴儿 RSV 的免疫产品获得批准。它们是两种长效单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗 和 clesrovimab,以及一种母体 RSV 疫苗。这些干预措施对就诊的 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染的疗效为 49% 至 76%,对因 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染而住院的疗效为 55% 至 91%。不同产品和随访时间的疗效各不相同。在获得许可后的真实世界证据研究中也报告了类似或更高的有效性。总体而言,这些干预措施的耐受性良好,且安全性良好。结论 新推出的长效单克隆抗体和母源RSV 疫苗已被证明具有高效性且安全性令人放心。这些措施已在许多国家实施,并大大减少了婴儿的呼吸道合胞病毒负担。

papers.title: Maternal RSVpreF Vaccine Effectiveness Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Hospitalized Infants
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: In February 2025, Australia introduced maternal vaccination with bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in the National Immunization Program for pregnant individuals from 28 weeks' gestation as the primary, year-round strategy to prevent RSV disease in infants 6 months of age or younger. OBJECTIVE: To estimate effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia with year-round respiratory testing for acute respiratory illness (ARI) among infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with ARI at 6 months of age or younger, March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026. Data were analyzed March 2026 through May 2026. EXPOSURE: Maternal RSVpreF vaccination administered from 28 weeks' gestation and 14 days or more before delivery. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Maternal RSVpreF effectiveness was evaluated against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD, primary objective), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI. Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had LRTD, with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers (median [IQR] gestational age at vaccination, 31 weeks [29-33]). Median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 32 years (29-35). Median (IQR) age of infants hospitalized for LRTD was 52 days (30-89); 495 of 655 (76%) were aged 3 months or younger. VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) among infants from birth through 3 months of age, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) among infants from birth through 2 months of age, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) among infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. Comparable VE among infants aged 6 months or younger was observed for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%; 95% CI, 54.4%-91.6%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%; 95% CI, 70.4%-87.6%) hospitalization, with similar age-specific trends. VE was consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination, vaccination to delivery time interval, and proximal administration with other vaccines during pregnancy. Descriptively, among all infants hospitalized with ARI, 161 of 499 (32%) born to RSVpreF-unvaccinated mothers had severe LRTD, while 87 of 513 (17%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers had severe LRTD. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings in this case-control study demonstrate high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in the first year following introduction in Australia, with the highest VE observed in the earliest age intervals. Future analyses with larger sample sizes will evaluate VE among additional subgroups.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in infants, and prior to 2025, no maternal vaccination strategy existed in Australia to prevent RSV disease in this vulnerable population. The study was needed to quantify the effectiveness of a newly introduced maternal RSV prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in preventing infant RSV hospitalization.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted across 9 hospitals in Australia, enrolling infants born at 28 weeks' gestation or later who were hospitalized with acute respiratory illness (ARI) at 6 months of age or younger between March 1, 2025, and February 28, 2026.
analysis.methods: Vaccine effectiveness (VE) was estimated using logistic regression with confounder adjustment, calculating VE as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100% against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI.
analysis.main_results: Among 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) overall, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) for infants aged 3 months or younger, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) for infants aged 2 months or younger, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) for infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates high year-round effectiveness of maternal RSVpreF vaccination in preventing RSV-associated hospitalization in infants under 6 months, with the highest protection observed in the earliest age intervals. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the continued use of maternal RSVpreF vaccination as a primary strategy to reduce RSV-related hospitalizations in infants, particularly in the first two months of life when risk is highest.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on hospital-based data, which may not capture all RSV cases in the community. Despite this, the large sample size and consistent VE estimates across multiple outcomes strengthen the evidence. Future analyses with larger sample sizes are planned to evaluate additional subgroups.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of maternal vaccination with the bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in preventing infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. Using a retrospective case-control design with a test-negative approach across nine hospitals, researchers analyzed data from 1,012 infants hospitalized with acute respiratory illness (ARI) aged 6 months or younger between March 2025 and February 2026. Vaccine effectiveness (VE) was calculated using logistic regression with confounder adjustment. The primary outcome, VE against RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD) hospitalization, was 77.8% overall, with higher protection observed in younger infants (86.3% for those aged 2 months or younger). Comparable VE was found for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%). VE remained consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination and timing of vaccination relative to delivery. The study concludes that maternal RSVpreF vaccination provides high year-round protection against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants under 6 months, particularly in early infancy, supporting its continued use as a national immunization strategy.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿住院的主要原因,2025 年之前,澳大利亚尚无孕产妇 呼吸道合胞病毒 策略来预防这一弱势群体的 RSV 疾病。该研究需要量化新引入的基于母体 RSV 预灌注 F 蛋白的 疫苗 (RSVpreF) 在预防婴儿 RSV 住院方面的有效性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在澳大利亚 9 家医院进行了一项采用测试阴性设计的回顾性病例对照研究,纳入了 2025 年 3 月 1 日至 2026 年 2 月 28 日期间因 6 个月以下急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 住院的妊娠 28 周或以后出生的婴儿。
elements_zh.methods: 疫苗 有效性 (VE) 使用逻辑回归和混杂因素调整进行估计,将 VE 计算为(1 - 调整后的比值比)× 100% 与 RSV 下呼吸道疾病 (RSV-LRTD)、严重 RSV-LRTD 和 RSV-ARI 住院治疗相比。
elements_zh.main_results: 在1012名因急性呼吸道感染住院的婴儿中,呼吸道合胞病毒下呼吸道疾病住院的疫苗保护效力为77.8%(95%置信区间,66.4%-85.3%),总体情况如下:3个月或更小婴儿为80.2%(95%置信区间,71.1%-86.5%)、2个月或更小婴儿为86.3%(95%置信区间,79.0%-91.1%)、年龄大于2个月至4个月的婴儿为68.2%(95%置信区间,42.2%-82.5%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,母亲 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 在预防 6 个月以下婴儿因 RSV 相关住院方面全年均具有很高的有效性,在最早的年龄间隔中观察到的保护效果最高。这是澳大利亚继全国推广后首次对孕产妇 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 有效性进行全年评估。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持继续使用母体 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 作为减少婴儿 RSV 相关住院的主要策略,特别是在风险最高的生命前两个月。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对医院数据的依赖而受到限制,这些数据可能无法涵盖社区中的所有 RSV 病例。尽管如此,大样本量和多种结果的一致的 VE 估计强化了证据。未来计划使用更大的样本量进行分析,以评估其他亚组。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿住院的主要原因,2025 年之前,澳大利亚尚无孕产妇 呼吸道合胞病毒 策略来预防这一弱势群体的 RSV 疾病。该研究需要量化新引入的基于母体 RSV 预灌注 F 蛋白的 疫苗 (RSVpreF) 在预防婴儿 RSV 住院方面的有效性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在澳大利亚 9 家医院进行了一项采用测试阴性设计的回顾性病例对照研究,纳入了 2025 年 3 月 1 日至 2026 年 2 月 28 日期间因 6 个月以下急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 住院的妊娠 28 周或以后出生的婴儿。
analysis_zh.methods: 疫苗 有效性 (VE) 使用逻辑回归和混杂因素调整进行估计,将 VE 计算为(1 - 调整后的比值比)× 100% 与 RSV 下呼吸道疾病 (RSV-LRTD)、严重 RSV-LRTD 和 RSV-ARI 住院治疗相比。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在1012名因急性呼吸道感染住院的婴儿中,呼吸道合胞病毒下呼吸道疾病住院的疫苗保护效力为77.8%(95%置信区间,66.4%-85.3%),总体情况如下:3个月或更小婴儿为80.2%(95%置信区间,71.1%-86.5%)、2个月或更小婴儿为86.3%(95%置信区间,79.0%-91.1%)、年龄大于2个月至4个月的婴儿为68.2%(95%置信区间,42.2%-82.5%)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,母亲 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 在预防 6 个月以下婴儿因 RSV 相关住院方面全年均具有很高的有效性,在最早的年龄间隔中观察到的保护效果最高。这是澳大利亚继全国推广后首次对孕产妇 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 有效性进行全年评估。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持继续使用母体 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 作为减少婴儿 RSV 相关住院的主要策略,特别是在风险最高的生命前两个月。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对医院数据的依赖而受到限制,这些数据可能无法涵盖社区中的所有 RSV 病例。尽管如此,大样本量和多种结果的一致的 VE 估计强化了证据。未来计划使用更大的样本量进行分析,以评估其他亚组。

However, reports in Japan are limited. We describe a rare case of bloodstream infection caused by Papiliotrema laurentii in a 4-year-old Japanese girl with cerebral palsy and epilepsy. She was diagnosed with respiratory syncytial virus- associated acute encephalopathy, and received methylprednisolone pulse therapy as part of intensive management. Despite completion of the 3-day steroid therapy, her fever persisted. Subsequent blood cultures performed 3 days after steroid therapy completion revealed the presence of yeast-like organisms. The isolate was identified as Papiliotrema laurentii using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer and D1/D2 regions. Antifungal susceptibility testing revealed a characteristic profile distinct from that of common yeasts. Micafungin was switched to liposomal amphotericin B and later to fosfluconazole, resulting in complete resolution. The patient remained relapse-free at the 6-month follow-up. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of Papiliotrema laurentii fungemia in Japan; however, its true incidence may be underestimated because of diagnostic limitations and limited surveillance data. This case suggests that methylprednisolone pulse therapy may predispose even immunocompetent children to opportunistic fungemia and that accurate identification and susceptibility testing are essential for appropriate antifungal management. Keywords: Acute encephalopathy; Antifungal susceptibility; Cryptococcus laurentii; Fungemia; Papiliotrema laurentii Accepted Manuscript 3 Introduction Papiliotrema laurentii (formerly Cryptococcus laurentii) has been increasingly recognized as a cause of invasive infections worldwide (Khawcharoenporn et al. 2007; Arendrup et al. 2014). Its antifungal susceptibility patterns differ from those of more common yeast pathogens (Pfaller et al. 2009; Bernal-Martinez et al. 2010). This environmental yeast is distributed globally (Mattsson et al. 1999; Filion et al. 2006; Andrade-Silva et al. 2010), including in East Asia (Jang et al. 2011), and often causes invasive diseases, primarily in individuals with impaired cellular immunity (Manfredi et al. 2006). Despite its widespread environmental presence, reports of P. laurentii infection in Japan are extremely scarce. To date, only a single case of peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis has been described (Asano et al. 2015), suggesting that invasive P. laurentii infections may be underdiagnosed in Japan. Methylprednisolone pulse therapy is commonly used in Japan for acute encephalopathy, according to the hypothesis that excessive inflammatory responses contribute to neurological injury (Omata and Takanashi 2025). However, the therapeutic efficacy of corticosteroids remains controversial; although they may be effective in the treatment of encephalopathy associated with hypercytokinemia (Okumura et al. 2009), their benefits for other pathological conditions have not been established (Hayashi et al. 2012). Because high-dose corticosteroids can transiently suppress cellular immunity, careful attention to the risk of opportunistic infections is warranted. Glucocorticoids exert immunosuppressive effects through multiple mechanisms, including inhibition of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling and proinflammatory cytokine production, reduced antigen presentation by dendritic cells, impaired monocyte–macrophage and T-cell Accepted Manuscript 4 function, and modulation of innate immune responses through epigenetic reprogramming and disruption of trained immunity. Collectively, these effects increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections (Cain and Cidlowski 2017). Herein, we report the first pediatric case of P. laurentii bloodstream infection, also known as fungemia, in Japan following methylprednisolone pulse therapy for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated acute encephalopathy. Informed consent for publication of this case report was obtained from the patient’s guardians. Case Presentation A 4-year-old Japanese girl with a history of severe neonatal asphyxia, hypoxic– ischemic encephalopathy, symptomatic epilepsy, status epilepticus associated with coronavirus disease 2019, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted to a local hospital for febrile seizures. Seizures were controlled with midazolam and thiopental; however, diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging revealed hyperintense lesions in the occipital lobes (Fig. 1A), with no corresponding signal changes on T2-weighted imaging/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery imaging (Fig. 1B). A rapid antigen test was positive for RSV, and she was diagnosed with RSV-associated acute encephalopathy before transfer to our tertiary care center. On admission, the neurological status of the patient was severely impaired, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of E1V2M4. Pupils measured 2.5 mm bilaterally, with intact light reflexes. She was febrile (38.8°C) and hemodynamically unstable, with a heart rate of 110 beats/min, blood pressure of 79/52 mmHg, prolonged capillary refill time of 4 s, and peripheral coldness. Respiratory findings included glossoptosis, diminished Accepted Manuscript 5 breathing sounds, and intercostal retractions. Initial laboratory evaluation showed elevated inflammatory markers: white blood cell count, 8,600/μL; C-reactive protein level, 3.05 mg/dL; aspartate aminotransferase level, 215 U/L; alanine aminotransferase level, 58 U/L; and procalcitonin level, 23.61 ng/mL. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed no pleocytosis, with protein 16 mg/dL and glucose 65 mg/dL. Gram staining and culture results were negative (Table 1). Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of nasal discharge, sputum, whole blood, serum, and cerebrospinal fluid yielded negative results for herpes simplex virus 1/2 and human herpesvirus 6. Human herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) was detected in aspirated sputum (1.66E+03 copies /mL) and whole blood (9.13E+03 copies /mL). In addition, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) identified RSV subtype A in nasopharyngeal swab (5.36E+09 copies /mL) and aspirated sputum (5.37E+09 copies /mL) specimens (Supplementary Table S1). Primers and probes used for the PCR and RT-PCR assays were those previously reported (Okabe et al. 2025). Electroencephalography demonstrated suppressed background activity attributable to sedative medications (Fig. 2). Chest radiography revealed atelectasis of the left upper lobe (Fig. 3), which contributed to the diagnosis of aspiration pneumonia. The patient was ultimately diagnosed with RSV-associated acute encephalopathy and acute pneumonia. She was intubated, mechanically ventilated, and managed in the pediatric intensive care unit. A central venous catheter was placed in the right femoral vein to secure a route for the administration of vasoactive agents. Normothermia therapy using an Arctic Sun device and methylprednisolone pulse therapy (30 mg/kg/day) were initiated. Mitochondrial cocktail therapy (ascorbic acid, benfotiamine, pyridoxine, Accepted Manuscript 6 cyanocobalamin, and carnitine) was also administered to support mitochondrial function in the context of possible metabolic encephalopathy (Omata and Takanashi 2025). Ampicillin/sulbactam (150 mg/kg/day) was administered to treat suspected aspiration pneumonia. Dopamine treatment was initiated to treat sedation-related hypotension. Methylprednisolone pulse therapy was administered for 3 days. Although active temperature management was stopped on day 4, the fever persisted. Oliguria developed on day 6, necessitating escalation of dopamine levels. On day 7, the central venous catheter was removed, and blood cultures were obtained. The fever resolved, and antibiotics were discontinued on day 10. After 80 h of incubation, yeast-like organisms were detected in one anaerobic blood culture bottle obtained via peripheral venipuncture (Fig. 4), whereas the catheter tip culture was negative. Candidemia was suspected based on the detection of yeast-like organisms in blood culture, and micafungin (2 mg/kg/day), a first-line empirical therapy for candidemia, was initiated on day 11. The patient was extubated on the same day that her respiratory status improved. On day 14, the isolate was identified as P. laurentii by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, with a confidence score of >2.0. Identification was confirmed by sequencing the internal transcribed spacer and D1/D2 regions, which showed 100% similarity with the reference sequence (GenBank accession no. KY108740.1). Subsequently, treatment was switched to liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day). On day 35, antifungal susceptibility testing was performed according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute standard M27 (4th edition) (CLSI 2017). Testing revealed characteristic minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs): micafungin, > 16 mg/L; amphotericin B, 1 mg/L; and fluconazole, 4 mg/L (Table 2). Consequently, Accepted Manuscript 7 therapy was de-escalated to fosfluconazole (5 mg/kg/day). Although clinical breakpoints have not been established for P. laurentii, the MIC values for amphotericin B and fluconazole were within the epidemiological cutoff values reported for Cryptococcus neoformans (Espinel-Ingroff et al. 2012). Antifungal treatment (liposomal amphotericin B and fosfluconazole) was continued for 28 days. Follow-up blood cultures obtained on days 11, 12, 14, and 22 were negative. Ophthalmologic examinations were performed on days 14, 21, and 28, and none of them revealed any evidence of endophthalmitis. The clinical course, including the timing of microbiological identification and antifungal treatment modification, is summarized in Figure 5. Considering steroid-related temporal immunosuppression, antifungal consolidation therapy was not administered. The patient was subsequently diagnosed with laryngomalacia and underwent tracheostomy. She was discharged from the pediatric intensive care unit on day 67 and transferred back to the referring hospital on day 78. She remained relapse-free at the 6-month follow-up. Discussion A salient feature of this case was the development of P. laurentii fungemia after methylprednisolone pulse therapy for RSV-associated acute encephalopathy. Blood cultures were positive for P. laurentii, confirming a diagnosis of fungemia. Based on antifungal susceptibility testing, we tailored the antifungal therapy to agents with expected activity against the isolate, resulting in successful treatment without relapse. This case report highlights two important clinical findings. First, P. laurentii fungemia, with atypical antifungal susceptibility patterns, can occur in Japan and should Accepted Manuscript 8 be considered in cases of bloodstream yeast infections. Second, methylprednisolone pulse therapy for acute encephalopathy may have been associated with the development of an opportunistic fungal infection in this case. P. laurentii fungemia has been reported in neonates (Cheng et al. 2001; Al-Otaibi et al. 2021; Gupta et al. 2018; Johnson et al. 1998), patients receiving chemotherapy (Londero et al. 2019), individuals with glomerulonephritis treated with corticosteroids (Furman-Kuklińska et al. 2009), and hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients (Park et al. 2017; Krcméry et al. 1997). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of P. laurentii fungemia complicating RSV-associated acute encephalopathy ever reported. Although this is the first reported case of P. laurentii fungemia in Japan, the apparent rarity may reflect underdiagnosis rather than true absence. P. laurentii can be misidentified as other yeast species using conventional diagnostic methods, and routine surveillance data for non-neoformans Cryptococcus species are limited. Therefore, the true incidence of P. laurentii infection in Japan may be underestimated. P. laurentii has been isolated from environmental samples including bird droppings, soil, and tree hollows in various geographic regions (Mattsson et al. 1999; Andrade-Silva et al. 2010; Jang et al. 2011; Sláviková and Vadkertiová 2003; Prakash et al. 2018). Notably, our patient had no history of exposure to birds or other environmental risk factors. This observation raises the hypothesis that P. laurentii is present in the general environment in Japan and can cause infection under conditions of transient immunosuppression. Although the patient had no underlying primary immunodeficiency, she was exposed to risk factors for fungemia, including transient impairment of cellular immunity induced by methylprednisolone pulse therapy and the presence of a central venous catheter (Khawcharoenporn et al. 2007). In addition, severe RSV infection, Accepted Manuscript 9 critical illness, immune dysregulation associated with systemic inflammation, and prolonged pediatric intensive care unit exposure may also have contributed to increased susceptibility to opportunistic fungal infection. Although the catheter tip culture was negative, the possibility that femoral venous catheterization contributed to fungal invasion cannot be excluded. Previous reports have shown that P. laurentii generally exhibits susceptibility to amphotericin B, whereas susceptibility to azoles is variable and echinocandins have limited activity (Pfaller et al. 2009; Bernal-Martinez et al. 2010). The limited activity of echinocandins against Cryptococcus species has been attributed to intrinsic resistance mechanisms despite the presence of β-1,3-D-glucan synthase as the antifungal target (Chen et al. 2011). These findings highlight the importance of accurate species identification for appropriate antifungal selection. HHV-7 was detected in this case, although its clinical significance remains uncertain. Herpes virus has been reported to modulate host immune responses, particularly affecting T-cell function, and may contribute to transient immunosuppression (Alibek et al. 2014). Although HHV-7 was detected in sputum and whole blood samples, the HHV-7 DNA level was low and HHV-7 was not detected in serum. On the basis of these findings, RSV was considered the primary etiological agent in this case. However, HHV-7 detection may represent viral reactivation, incidental detection, or a potential contributor to the encephalopathic presentation, and these possibilities cannot be excluded. A limitation of this report is that the antifungal susceptibility of P. laurentii was interpreted with reference to epidemiological cutoff values for C. neoformans. Although these species are phylogenetically related, differences in susceptibility profiles across species may limit the validity of this extrapolation. Accepted Manuscript 10 In conclusion, we report the first case of P. laurentii fungemia in Japan that occurred after methylprednisolone pulse therapy for RSV-associated acute encephalopathy. Clinicians should recognize that P. laurentii has a unique antifungal susceptibility profile and that high-dose corticosteroid therapy may increase the risk of fungemia, even in children without chronic immunodeficiency. This case highlights the importance of considering opportunistic fungal infections and performing early fungal surveillance in patients with persistent fever following immunosuppressive therapy. In addition, advanced diagnostic tools such as matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and molecular sequencing may facilitate accurate identification of rare pathogens and guide appropriate antifungal therapy. Careful risk– benefit assessment of methylprednisolone pulse therapy and vigilance for opportunistic infections are essential when managing persistent fever after immunosuppressive therapy. papers.abstract_original: Papiliotrema laurentii is an environmental yeast that has been increasingly recognized as a cause of invasive infections, particularly in individuals with impaired cellular immunity.However, reports in Japan are limited.We describe a rare case of bloodstream infection caused by Papiliotrema laurentii in a 4-year-old Japanese girl with cerebral palsy and epilepsy.She was diagnosed with respiratory syncytial virusassociated acute encephalopathy, and received methylprednisolone pulse therapy as part of intensive management.Despite completion of the 3-day steroid therapy, her fever persisted.Subsequent blood cultures performed 3 days after steroid therapy completion revealed the presence of yeast-like organisms.The isolate was identified as Papiliotrema laurentii using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer and D1/D2 regions.Antifungal susceptibility testing revealed a characteristic profile distinct from that of common yeasts.Micafungin was switched to liposomal amphotericin B and later to fosfluconazole, resulting in complete resolution.The patient remained relapse-free at the 6-month follow-up.To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of Papiliotrema laurentii fungemia in Japan; however, its true incidence may be underestimated because of diagnostic limitations and limited surveillance data.This case suggests that methylprednisolone pulse therapy may predispose even immunocompetent children to opportunistic fungemia and that accurate identification and susceptibility testing are essential for appropriate antifungal management.
papers.title_original: Papiliotrema Laurentii Bloodstream Infection Following Methylprednisolone Pulse Therapy for Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Associated Acute Encephalopathy in a Child.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 4-year-old Japanese girl with cerebral palsy and epilepsy who developed Papiliotrema laurentii bloodstream infection following methylprednisolone pulse therapy for respiratory syncytial virus-associated acute encephalopathy. The organism was identified using mass spectrometry and sequencing, and antifungal susceptibility testing guided a switch from micafungin to liposomal amphotericin B and fosfluconazole, resulting in clinical resolution and no relapse at 6 months. This is the first reported case of Papiliotrema laurentii fungemia in Japan, suggesting that methylprednisolone pulse therapy may predispose children to opportunistic fungemia. The findings highlight the importance of accurate identification and susceptibility testing for appropriate antifungal management and underscore the need for improved surveillance and diagnostic capacity to detect rare fungal pathogens in immunocompromised patients.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 劳伦凤蝶(Papiliotrema laurentii)是一种环境酵母,越来越多地被认为是免疫功能低下个体侵袭性感染的原因,但日本的报道有限。该研究需要记录一名因 呼吸道合胞病毒 相关急性脑病而接受甲泼尼龙冲击治疗的儿童发生劳伦凤蝶血流感染的罕见病例。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一名患有脑瘫和癫痫的 4 岁日本女孩 病例报告 的单例患者,她在接受 呼吸道合胞病毒 相关急性脑病的甲泼尼龙冲击治疗后出现劳伦凤蝶真菌血症。
elements_zh.methods: 使用基质辅助激光解吸/电离飞行时间质谱法以及内部转录间隔区和 D1/D2 区域的测序来鉴定分离物。进行抗真菌药敏试验,根据药敏结果将治疗由米卡芬净调整为脂质体两性霉素B,随后调整为氟康唑。
elements_zh.main_results: 完成 3 天类固醇治疗后 3 天进行的血培养显示出酵母样生物,后来证实为 Papiliotrema laurentii。抗真菌敏感性测试显示出与普通酵母不同的特征。患者在 6 个月的随访中完全康复并保持无复发。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这是日本首例报告的劳氏凤蝶真菌血症病例,凸显了甲基泼尼松龙脉冲疗法甚至可能使免疫功能正常的儿童易患机会性真菌血症。准确的鉴定和药敏测试对于适当的抗真菌管理至关重要。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例强调了在接受免疫抑制治疗的儿童中需要提高对罕见真菌病原体的临床认识,以及指导抗真菌药物 治疗 的精确诊断方法的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这限制了普遍性并排除了因果推断。诊断局限性和漏报可能导致低估 Papiliotrema laurentii 发病率,需要提高 监测 和诊断能力。

papers.abstract_zh: 劳伦凤蝶是一种环境酵母菌,越来越多地被认为是侵袭性感染的原因,特别是在细胞免疫受损的个体中。然而,日本的报道有限。我们描述了一名患有脑瘫和癫痫的 4 岁日本女孩,由劳伦凤蝶引起的血流感染的罕见病例。她被诊断患有呼吸道合胞病毒相关急性脑病,并接受甲泼尼龙冲击治疗作为强化治疗的一部分尽管完成了 3 天的类固醇治疗,她的发烧仍然持续。类固醇治疗完成 3 天后进行的后续血培养显示存在酵母样生物体。使用基质辅助激光解吸/电离飞行时间质谱和内部转录间隔区和 D1/D2 区域的测序,将该分离株鉴定为 Papiliotrema laurentii。抗真菌药敏测试显示其特征谱与常见的不同。米卡芬净改用脂质体两性霉素 B,后来改用氟康唑,病情完全缓解。6 个月随访后,患者未复发。据我们所知,这是日本首例报道的凤蝶真菌血症病例;然而,由于诊断局限性和有限的 发病率 数据,其真实的 发病率 可能被低估。该病例表明,甲泼尼龙冲击治疗甚至可能使免疫功能正常的儿童易患机会性真菌血症,准确的识别和药敏测试对于适当的抗真菌治疗至关重要。

papers.title: Kinetics and characterization of extracellular vesicle release from cells infected with a clinical isolate of respiratory syncytial virus A (ON1 genotype)
papers.abstract: Abstract Despite the recent approval of preventive measures, the disease burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children and older adults remains significant. To improve understanding of RSV disease, this study characterized extracellular microvesicles (EMVs) secreted during in vitro infection with a clinical RSV-A (ON1 genotype) strain (RSV/40G-A), isolated in 2022 from a pediatric pneumonia case. The type and content of EMVs released by A549 and BEAS-2B respiratory epithelial cells infected with this clinical isolate were analyzed up to 96 h post-infection (hpi). RSV infection induced a time-dependent increase in EMV levels compared to uninfected controls. EMVs released by infected BEAS-2B and A549 cells contained increasing levels of RSV nucleocapsid protein (RSV-NP) and viral RNA with a peak at 72 hpi. These findings suggest that the kinetics of vesicular release and EMV content are modulated during RSV infection. EMV secretion by host cells may constitute a potential mechanism for intercellular communication or immune activation.

papers.title: Respiratory syncytial virus outbreaks in healthcare facilities: A review of the literature.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory infections. Outbreaks have occurred in various healthcare settings. We reviewed RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. PubMed was searched from 2010 to 2025 for articles on RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. Eighteen articles presenting 19 RSV outbreaks were reviewed. Eleven outbreaks occurred in hematology/oncology/transplantation wards/units, six in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), and two in geriatric hospitals/long-term care facilities (LTCFs). The mean attack rate across all outbreaks was 26.04% (range: 12.00%-68.96%) and the mean duration was 39.9 (range: 5-131) days. A mean of 20.31 (range: 4-63) patients were affected per outbreak. Asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare personnel (HCP) were the most frequent sources of infection. RSV disease was particularly severe in premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients. Prolonged virus shedding also occurred among premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients, challenging the containment of outbreaks. The overall case fatality rate (CFR) among RSV-infected patients was 11.64% (mean CFR: 13.99% in hematology/oncology/transplantation units, 6.49% in NICUs, and 6.25% in geriatric clinics). Palivizumab prophylaxis was temporally associated with outbreak control when used as part of multimodal interventions. In conclusion, serious RSV outbreaks occur in healthcare facilities caring for vulnerable patients. Such outbreaks are frequently traced to HCP, usually last several weeks, and affect many patients, which emphasize the transmission dynamics of RSV within healthcare facilities but also disclose gaps in infection control. Elderly patients, residents of LTCFs, and immunocompromised patients should be vaccinated against RSV. Palivizumab prophylaxis should be studied.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; Orthopneumovirus hominis, including RSV-A and RSV-B) outbreaks in healthcare facilities, focusing on vulnerable patient populations such as premature neonates, immunosuppressed patients, and elderly residents of long-term care facilities. The central question addresses the transmission dynamics, severity, and control of RSV outbreaks within these settings.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that searched PubMed from 2010 to 2025 for articles on RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. Eighteen articles presenting 19 outbreaks were included, covering hematology/oncology/transplantation wards (11 outbreaks), neonatal intensive care units (6 outbreaks), and geriatric hospitals/long-term care facilities (2 outbreaks).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities are frequent, often traced to asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare personnel, and typically last several weeks. The mean attack rate across outbreaks was 26.04% (range: 12.00%-68.96%), with a mean duration of 39.9 days (range: 5-131 days). The overall case fatality rate among infected patients was 11.64%, with higher rates in hematology/oncology/transplantation units (13.99%) compared to neonatal intensive care units (6.49%) and geriatric clinics (6.25%).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Prolonged virus shedding in premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients challenges outbreak containment, and the review highlights gaps in infection control practices. The evidence base is limited to 19 outbreaks across specific high-risk settings, leaving uncertainty about transmission dynamics in other healthcare environments and populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Priority research should investigate the role of asymptomatic healthcare personnel in RSV transmission and evaluate multimodal interventions, including palivizumab prophylaxis, for outbreak control. Enhanced surveillance and infection control measures are needed in high-risk units, particularly for elderly and immunocompromised patients, to reduce outbreak severity and mortality.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) outbreaks in healthcare facilities, focusing on vulnerable populations such as premature neonates, immunosuppressed patients, and elderly residents. Across 19 outbreaks, RSV demonstrated high attack rates (mean 26.04%) and prolonged durations (mean 39.9 days), with healthcare personnel often serving as asymptomatic sources. The overall case fatality rate was 11.64%, with the highest burden in hematology/oncology/transplantation units. Key gaps include challenges in containing outbreaks due to prolonged shedding in high-risk patients and limited evidence from diverse healthcare settings. Research priorities include investigating transmission dynamics, evaluating multimodal interventions like palivizumab, and strengthening infection control in high-risk units.

papers.source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory infections. Outbreaks have occurred in various healthcare settings. We reviewed RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. PubMed was searched from 2010 to 2025 for articles on RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. Eighteen articles presenting 19 RSV outbreaks were reviewed. Eleven outbreaks occurred in hematology/oncology/transplantation wards/units, six in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), and two in geriatric hospitals/long-term care facilities (LTCFs). The mean attack rate across all outbreaks was 26.04% (range: 12.00%-68.96%) and the mean duration was 39.9 (range: 5-131) days. A mean of 20.31 (range: 4-63) patients were affected per outbreak. Asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare personnel (HCP) were the most frequent sources of infection. RSV disease was particularly severe in premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients. Prolonged virus shedding also occurred among premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients, challenging the containment of outbreaks. The overall case fatality rate (CFR) among RSV-infected patients was 11.64% (mean CFR: 13.99% in hematology/oncology/transplantation units, 6.49% in NICUs, and 6.25% in geriatric clinics). Palivizumab prophylaxis was temporally associated with outbreak control when used as part of multimodal interventions. In conclusion, serious RSV outbreaks occur in healthcare facilities caring for vulnerable patients. Such outbreaks are frequently traced to HCP, usually last several weeks, and affect many patients, which emphasize the transmission dynamics of RSV within healthcare facilities but also disclose gaps in infection control. Elderly patients, residents of LTCFs, and immunocompromised patients should be vaccinated against RSV. Palivizumab prophylaxis should be studied.

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Adults in India: An Under-recognized Public Health Concern Demanding Urgent Immunization Action.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important global cause of acute respiratory tract infection, contributing substantially to illness, hospitalization, and deaths across all age groups worldwide. While RSV has long been associated with severe disease in infants and young children, its impact on older adults is increasingly recognized, with evidence suggesting that mortality in elderly populations may equal or exceed that in paediatric age groups. In India, demographic transition, increasing prevalence of chronic comorbidities, and limited adult vaccination programmes are likely to amplify the burden of RSV disease, which remains under-recognized and insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The article delineates the burden of RSV among Indian adults, assesses current evidence and regulatory status of RSV vaccines, and identifies priorities for strengthening surveillance, informing policy, and advancing immunization efforts. CONTENT: Although national adult-specific RSV data from India remain scarce, available evidence indicates that RSV is an important contributor to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized adults, with a substantial disease burden among older adults in India. Three vaccines-GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo and Moderna mRNA-1345 are currently approved for adults ≥60 years in the United States and Europe. Early real world data from United Kingdom demonstrates significant reduction in RSV related hospitalizations following vaccine introduction within a single season [19]. In India, CDSCO conditionally approved Phase III trials of RSVPreF in June 2025, but no adult RSV vaccine is licensed for use. This review proposes for integration of routine RSV molecular testing and reporting with outcome especially in comorbid adults, inclusion of RSV vaccination in National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI) deliberations for elder and high-risk groups, accelerated regulatory pathways leveraging global bridging data and implementation of prospective multicenter studies to generate robust evidence for health technology assessment, cost-effectiveness and policy formulation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV is a major global cause of acute respiratory tract infections with substantial morbidity and mortality across all age groups, yet its burden in older adults and in India remains under-characterized and under-recognized. The study addresses the knowledge gap regarding RSV disease burden among Indian adults and the regulatory status of adult RSV vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a narrative review that synthesizes existing evidence on RSV burden in Indian adults and evaluates the regulatory landscape of adult RSV vaccines. It focuses on hospitalized adults, particularly older adults with comorbidities, and discusses surveillance priorities and policy needs in India.
analysis.methods: The review integrates published evidence on RSV epidemiology in adults, regulatory approvals of RSV vaccines in other regions, and real-world effectiveness data from the United Kingdom. It proposes integration of routine RSV molecular testing, inclusion of RSV vaccination in national immunization deliberations, and implementation of multicenter studies to generate robust evidence.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights that RSV contributes substantially to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized Indian adults, with a notable burden among older adults. It notes that three vaccines (GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo, Moderna mRNA-1345) are approved for adults aged 60 years and older in the United States and Europe, and that India has conditionally approved Phase III trials for RSVPreF but no adult RSV vaccine is currently licensed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that RSV in Indian adults is under-recognized and likely underestimated, particularly in high-risk groups, and emphasize the urgent need for strengthened surveillance, policy integration, and vaccine deployment. The novelty lies in synthesizing Indian-specific gaps and proposing actionable steps for surveillance and immunization.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritizing RSV molecular testing in comorbid adults, including RSV vaccination in national immunization policy deliberations, and accelerating regulatory pathways leveraging global data to inform health technology assessment and cost-effectiveness analyses in India.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base relies on a narrative review of limited national adult-specific data from India, which constrains generalizability and precision. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of robust, India-specific adult RSV burden estimates and the reliance on extrapolated data from other regions.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines the burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among adults in India, highlighting its under-recognition and substantial contribution to severe acute respiratory infections, particularly in older adults with comorbidities. The authors synthesize evidence on RSV epidemiology, regulatory approvals of adult RSV vaccines in other regions, and real-world effectiveness data, noting that three vaccines are approved for adults aged 60 years and older in the United States and Europe. In India, Phase III trials for RSVPreF have been conditionally approved, but no adult RSV vaccine is currently licensed. The review emphasizes the urgent need for strengthened surveillance, integration of RSV molecular testing in high-risk groups, inclusion of RSV vaccination in national immunization policy deliberations, and accelerated regulatory pathways leveraging global data. While the findings underscore the importance of addressing RSV in Indian adults, the evidence base is limited by scarce national adult-specific data, resulting in a moderate strength of evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: RSV 是全球急性呼吸道感染的一个主要原因,在所有年龄段都有很高的发病率和 死亡率,但其在老年人和印度的负担仍然未被充分描述和认识。该研究解决了印度成年人 RSV 疾病负担和成人 RSV 疫苗 监管状况方面的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一篇叙述性综述,综合了印度成人 RSV 负担的现有证据,并评估了成人 RSV 疫苗 的监管环境。它重点关注住院成人,特别是患有合并症的老年人,并讨论了印度的 监测 优先事项和政策需求。
elements_zh.methods: 该审查整合了已发表的关于成人 RSV 流行病学 的证据、其他地区对 RSV 疫苗 的监管批准以及来自英国的真实有效性数据。它建议整合常规 RSV 分子检测,将 RSV 疫苗接种 纳入国家免疫审议,并实施多中心研究以产生强有力的证据。
elements_zh.main_results: 该审查强调,RSV 在很大程度上导致印度住院成人严重急性呼吸道感染,对老年人造成了显着的负担。它指出,三种 疫苗(GSK Arexvy、辉瑞 Abrysvo、Moderna mRNA-1345)在美国和欧洲被批准用于 60 岁及以上的成年人,印度已有条件批准 RSVPreF 的 III 期试验,但目前没有成人 RSV 疫苗 获得许可。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为印度成年人中 RSV 未被充分认识和可能被低估的证据,特别是在高危人群中,并强调迫切需要加强 监测、政策整合和 疫苗 部署。新颖之处在于综合了印度特有的差距并提出了 监测 和免疫接种的可行步骤。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在国家免疫政策审议中优先考虑对共病成人进行 RSV 分子检测,包括 RSV 疫苗接种,并加快利用全球数据的监管途径,为印度的卫生技术评估和成本效益分析提供信息。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: RSV is a major global cause of acute respiratory tract infections with substantial morbidity and mortality across all age groups, yet its burden in older adults and in India remains under-characterized and under-recognized. The study addresses the knowledge gap regarding RSV disease burden among Indian adults and the regulatory status of adult RSV vaccines.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This is a narrative review that synthesizes existing evidence on RSV burden in Indian adults and evaluates the regulatory landscape of adult RSV vaccines. It focuses on hospitalized adults, particularly older adults with comorbidities, and discusses surveillance priorities and policy needs in India.
analysis_en.methods: The review integrates published evidence on RSV epidemiology in adults, regulatory approvals of RSV vaccines in other regions, and real-world effectiveness data from the United Kingdom. It proposes integration of routine RSV molecular testing, inclusion of RSV vaccination in national immunization deliberations, and implementation of multicenter studies to generate robust evidence.
analysis_en.main_results: The review highlights that RSV contributes substantially to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized Indian adults, with a notable burden among older adults. It notes that three vaccines (GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo, Moderna mRNA-1345) are approved for adults aged 60 years and older in the United States and Europe, and that India has conditionally approved Phase III trials for RSVPreF but no adult RSV vaccine is currently licensed.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that RSV in Indian adults is under-recognized and likely underestimated, particularly in high-risk groups, and emphasize the urgent need for strengthened surveillance, policy integration, and vaccine deployment. The novelty lies in synthesizing Indian-specific gaps and proposing actionable steps for surveillance and immunization.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritizing RSV molecular testing in comorbid adults, including RSV vaccination in national immunization policy deliberations, and accelerating regulatory pathways leveraging global data to inform health technology assessment and cost-effectiveness analyses in India.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base relies on a narrative review of limited national adult-specific data from India, which constrains generalizability and precision. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of robust, India-specific adult RSV burden estimates and the reliance on extrapolated data from other regions.

papers.title_zh: 印度成人中的 呼吸道合胞病毒:一个未被充分认识的公共卫生问题,需要采取紧急免疫行动。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important global cause of acute respiratory tract infection, contributing substantially to illness, hospitalization, and deaths across all age groups worldwide. While RSV has long been associated with severe disease in infants and young children, its impact on older adults is increasingly recognized, with evidence suggesting that mortality in elderly populations may equal or exceed that in paediatric age groups. In India, demographic transition, increasing prevalence of chronic comorbidities, and limited adult vaccination programmes are likely to amplify the burden of RSV disease, which remains under-recognized and insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The article delineates the burden of RSV among Indian adults, assesses current evidence and regulatory status of RSV vaccines, and identifies priorities for strengthening surveillance, informing policy, and advancing immunization efforts. CONTENT: Although national adult-specific RSV data from India remain scarce, available evidence indicates that RSV is an important contributor to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized adults, with a substantial disease burden among older adults in India. Three vaccines-GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo and Moderna mRNA-1345 are currently approved for adults ≥60 years in the United States and Europe. Early real world data from United Kingdom demonstrates significant reduction in RSV related hospitalizations following vaccine introduction within a single season [19]. In India, CDSCO conditionally approved Phase III trials of RSVPreF in June 2025, but no adult RSV vaccine is licensed for use. This review proposes for integration of routine RSV molecular testing and reporting with outcome especially in comorbid adults, inclusion of RSV vaccination in National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI) deliberations for elder and high-risk groups, accelerated regulatory pathways leveraging global bridging data and implementation of prospective multicenter studies to generate robust evidence for health technology assessment, cost-effectiveness and policy formulation.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是全球急性呼吸道感染的重要原因,在很大程度上导致全球所有年龄段的疾病、住院和死亡。虽然 RSV 长期以来一直与婴儿和幼儿的严重疾病相关,但人们越来越认识到它对老年人的影响,有证据表明老年人群中的 死亡率 可能等于或超过儿科年龄组的 死亡率。在印度,人口结构转变、慢性合并症 患病率 的增加以及成人 疫苗接种 计划的有限可能会加剧 RSV 疾病的负担,而 RSV 疾病仍然未被充分认识和充分表征。目标:本文描述了印度成年人中 RSV 的负担,评估了 RSV 疫苗 的当前证据和监管状况,并确定了加强 疫苗、为政策提供信息和推进免疫工作的优先事项。内容:尽管印度全国成人特定 RSV 数据仍然稀缺,但现有证据表明,RSV 是住院成人严重急性呼吸道感染的重要诱因,给印度老年人带来了巨大的疾病负担。疫苗-GSK Arexvy、辉瑞 Abrysvo 和 Moderna mRNA-1345 三种药物目前已在美国和欧洲获批用于 60 岁以上成人。来自英国的早期真实世界数据表明,在 疫苗 引入后,单一季节内 RSV 相关住院率显着减少 [19]。在印度,CDSCO 于 2025 年 6 月有条件批准了 RSVPreF 的 III 期试验,但没有成人 RSV 疫苗 获得使用许可。本次审查建议将常规 RSV 分子检测和报告与结果相结合,特别是在合并症成人中,将 RSV 疫苗接种 纳入国家免疫技术咨询组 (NTAGI) 对老年人和高危人群的审议,加速利用全球桥接数据的监管途径,并实施前瞻性多中心研究,为卫生技术评估、成本效益和政策制定提供强有力的证据。

papers.title: Live human metapneumovirus vaccine candidates attenuated by temperature sensitivity mutations from human respiratory syncytial virus
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human metapneumovirus (HMPV, genus Metapneumovirus ) and respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV, genus Orthopneumovirus ) are pediatric respiratory pathogens of the Pneumoviridae family. We previously developed live-intranasal HRSV vaccine candidates attenuated by genetically stabilized temperature sensitivity/attenuating ( ts/att ) mutations in the HRSV polymerase (L) ORF, including sites “ 1030s ” (L codon changes S1313 (AGC-to-TCA) /Y1321K (AAA) , named after clone number 1030), and “Δ1313/I1314L,” comprising a genetically stabilized deletion of L codon 1313. In pediatric vaccine studies, HRSV candidates with “ 1030s ” or Δ1313/I1314L were attenuated, immunogenic, and genetically stable. Given the similarities between HRSV and HMPV, we introduced corresponding modifications into the HMPV L ORF, resulting in HMPV with deletion of codon 1238 (Δ1238), corresponding to HRSV Δ1313/I1314L, and HMPV with C1238S (TCA) /Y1246K (AAA) substitutions together (C1238S/Y1246K, corresponding to HRSV “ 1030s ”), or individually (C1238S, Y1246K), serving as experimental controls. All versions replicated well in Vero cells at 32°C. At 37°C, replication of Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, and Y1246K was delayed, and peak titers were ~80-fold, 200-fold, and 25-fold lower than wild-type HMPV. As predicted, the C1238S control was not temperature-sensitive (shutoff temperature [ T SH ] > 40°C, similar to wild-type HMPV), while Y1246K and Δ1238 ( T SH = 39°C) and C1238S/Y1246K ( T SH = 38°C) had a ts phenotype. Thus, the addition of the C1238S (TCA) substitution increased the temperature sensitivity of Y1246K. The HMPV ts/att sites were genetically stable under temperature stress. In hamsters inoculated intranasally, C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 were restricted in replication, yet immunogenic and protective against HMPV challenge. Thus, inclusion in the HMPV L ORF of C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 mutations, corresponding to HRSV ts/att sites, provided genetically stable live-attenuated HMPV, suitable for clinical development. IMPORTANCE Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory illness in young children, and there are no licensed vaccines. Similarly to immunization strategies against the related human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV), live-attenuated HMPV vaccines for intranasal immunization would be most suitable for young children. Live-intranasal vaccines infect and induce immunity in the presence of residual maternal antibodies without priming for enhanced respiratory disease. Genetic stability of attenuating mutations represents a challenge in vaccine design. We generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing into corresponding sites of the HMPV polymerase gene temperature-sensitivity-inducing attenuating mutations that had been originally developed for HRSV, genetically stabilized, and proven to be free of reversions in HRSV vaccine studies. The resulting HMPV vaccine candidates are temperature-sensitive, attenuated, and genetically stable under temperature stress. In the hamster model, the new HMPV candidates were immunogenic and protective. These live-attenuated HMPV candidates will be advanced to pediatric vaccine studies.

papers.title_original: Live human metapneumovirus vaccine candidates attenuated by temperature sensitivity mutations from human respiratory syncytial virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory illness in young children, and there are no licensed vaccines. Given the similarities between HMPV and the related human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV), the study aimed to develop live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations originally developed for HRSV into the HMPV polymerase gene.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations into the HMPV polymerase (L) ORF, including Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, C1238S, and Y1246K. Replication and genetic stability were assessed in Vero cells at 32°C and 37°C, and the immunogenicity and protective efficacy were evaluated in hamsters inoculated intranasally.
analysis.methods: HMPV vaccine candidates were engineered by introducing HRSV-derived temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations into the HMPV L ORF, including Δ1238 (corresponding to HRSV Δ1313/I1314L) and C1238S/Y1246K (corresponding to HRSV “1030s”). Replication kinetics were measured in Vero cells at 32°C and 37°C, and temperature sensitivity was determined by shutoff temperature (T_SH). Genetic stability was assessed under temperature stress, and immunogenicity and protection were evaluated in hamsters after intranasal inoculation.
analysis.main_results: At 37°C, replication of Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, and Y1246K was delayed, with peak titers approximately 80-fold, 200-fold, and 25-fold lower than wild-type HMPV, respectively. The C1238S control was not temperature-sensitive (T_SH > 40°C), while Y1246K and Δ1238 (T_SH = 39°C) and C1238S/Y1246K (T_SH = 38°C) exhibited a temperature-sensitive phenotype. The C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 candidates were restricted in replication in hamsters but were immunogenic and protective against HMPV challenge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The introduction of HRSV-derived temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations into the HMPV L ORF generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates that are temperature-sensitive, attenuated, genetically stable, immunogenic, and protective in a hamster model. This approach leverages previously validated HRSV mutations, demonstrating a novel strategy for HMPV vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the advancement of live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates to pediatric clinical studies, offering a potential solution to the unmet need for HMPV vaccination in young children. The genetically stable temperature-sensitive mutations provide a robust platform for further development and evaluation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro and in a hamster model, which may not fully recapitulate human infection or immune responses. While the temperature-sensitive mutations were genetically stable under temperature stress, their stability and safety in humans remain to be confirmed. The evidence strength is moderate due to the preclinical nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed live-attenuated human metapneumovirus (HMPV) vaccine candidates by introducing temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations originally derived from human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) into the HMPV polymerase gene. Engineered candidates, including Δ1238 and C1238S/Y1246K, exhibited temperature-sensitive replication in vitro, with peak titers at 37°C reduced by 25- to 200-fold compared to wild-type HMPV. In hamsters, these candidates were restricted in replication yet induced immunogenicity and protection against HMPV challenge. The mutations were genetically stable under temperature stress, supporting their suitability for clinical development. These findings highlight a novel strategy for HMPV vaccine design, leveraging validated HRSV attenuating mutations, and justify advancing the candidates to pediatric vaccine studies.

papers.title_zh: 活人类偏肺病毒 疫苗 候选物因来自人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 的温度敏感性 突变 减毒
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human metapneumovirus (HMPV, genus Metapneumovirus ) and respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV, genus Orthopneumovirus ) are pediatric respiratory pathogens of the Pneumoviridae family. We previously developed live-intranasal HRSV vaccine candidates attenuated by genetically stabilized temperature sensitivity/attenuating ( ts/att ) mutations in the HRSV polymerase (L) ORF, including sites “ 1030s ” (L codon changes S1313 (AGC-to-TCA) /Y1321K (AAA) , named after clone number 1030), and “Δ1313/I1314L,” comprising a genetically stabilized deletion of L codon 1313. In pediatric vaccine studies, HRSV candidates with “ 1030s ” or Δ1313/I1314L were attenuated, immunogenic, and genetically stable. Given the similarities between HRSV and HMPV, we introduced corresponding modifications into the HMPV L ORF, resulting in HMPV with deletion of codon 1238 (Δ1238), corresponding to HRSV Δ1313/I1314L, and HMPV with C1238S (TCA) /Y1246K (AAA) substitutions together (C1238S/Y1246K, corresponding to HRSV “ 1030s ”), or individually (C1238S, Y1246K), serving as experimental controls. All versions replicated well in Vero cells at 32°C. At 37°C, replication of Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, and Y1246K was delayed, and peak titers were ~80-fold, 200-fold, and 25-fold lower than wild-type HMPV. As predicted, the C1238S control was not temperature-sensitive (shutoff temperature [ T SH ] > 40°C, similar to wild-type HMPV), while Y1246K and Δ1238 ( T SH = 39°C) and C1238S/Y1246K ( T SH = 38°C) had a ts phenotype. Thus, the addition of the C1238S (TCA) substitution increased the temperature sensitivity of Y1246K. The HMPV ts/att sites were genetically stable under temperature stress. In hamsters inoculated intranasally, C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 were restricted in replication, yet immunogenic and protective against HMPV challenge. Thus, inclusion in the HMPV L ORF of C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 mutations, corresponding to HRSV ts/att sites, provided genetically stable live-attenuated HMPV, suitable for clinical development. IMPORTANCE Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory illness in young children, and there are no licensed vaccines. Similarly to immunization strategies against the related human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV), live-attenuated HMPV vaccines for intranasal immunization would be most suitable for young children. Live-intranasal vaccines infect and induce immunity in the presence of residual maternal antibodies without priming for enhanced respiratory disease. Genetic stability of attenuating mutations represents a challenge in vaccine design. We generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing into corresponding sites of the HMPV polymerase gene temperature-sensitivity-inducing attenuating mutations that had been originally developed for HRSV, genetically stabilized, and proven to be free of reversions in HRSV vaccine studies. The resulting HMPV vaccine candidates are temperature-sensitive, attenuated, and genetically stable under temperature stress. In the hamster model, the new HMPV candidates were immunogenic and protective. These live-attenuated HMPV candidates will be advanced to pediatric vaccine studies.

papers.title: Household Transmission Dynamics of Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus in China: A Multicentre Epidemiological and Molecular Study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To estimate the secondary HRSV infection proportion, age-specific susceptibility, inferred spread, and HRSV-A/B transmission patterns in Chinese households. METHODS: This prospective case-ascertained household cohort in Zhejiang, China (November 2024-December 2025) recruited medically attended, laboratory-confirmed paediatric HRSV index cases aged 0-14 years. Ten-day exposure histories, Day 3/10 contact sampling, and regression models assessed household- and contact-level risk factors. RESULTS: Among 179 households with 542 contacts, secondary infection was detected in 110 households (61.5%) and 218 contacts (40.2%); 46.3% were symptomatic. Children aged 0-5 years accounted for 86.6% (155/179) of inferred primary cases. Contact infection was highest among children aged 0-5 years (86.4% [38/44]), including all infants aged <1 year (17/17). HRSV-B-only households had higher contact-level infection odds than HRSV-A-only households (aOR 1.96, 95% CI 1.05-3.65). Concordance of sequences from the second hypervariable region (HVR2) of the G gene supported household clustering (97.7% [84/86]). CONCLUSIONS: Children aged 0-5 years were the main inferred household introducers and were highly susceptible, with infants aged <1 year the most susceptible. Household transmission frequently involved spread from children aged 0-5 years to adults, supporting age-targeted household prevention.

papers.title: An evaluation of the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus activity of sophora alkaloids and the enhanced efficacy by liposomes via intratracheal administration
papers.abstract: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity of sophora alkaloids, particularly sophocarpine (SC), and their enhanced efficacy when encapsulated in liposomes via intratracheal administration. Liposomal encapsulation of SC significantly improved therapeutic outcomes by enhancing pulmonary retention and outperforming free SC in suppressing viral replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation. These findings provide a novel approach for RSV treatment, potentially addressing the challenges posed by the virus's high mutation rate and the limitations of existing antiviral drugs.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿、幼儿和老年人严重下呼吸道感染和相关死亡的主要原因。由于 RSV 的高 突变 发生率以及现有 抗病毒药物 药物的疗效和安全性有限,RSV 的临床管理具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 RSV 感染的小鼠模型进行体内研究,以评估槐树生物碱及其脂质体制剂的抗 RSV 活性。
elements_zh.methods: 槐生物碱,特别是槐果碱 (SC),被封装在脂质体中以增强肺滞留和治疗效果。作用机制涉及通过调节 MEK/ERK 信号通路抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化。
elements_zh.main_results: 体内研究表明,槐花生物碱通过气管内给药可显着降低 RSV 感染小鼠的 死亡率。在小鼠模型中,负载 SC 的脂质体在抑制 RSV 复制和减轻肺部炎症方面优于游离 SC。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究阐明,槐花生物碱通过抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化、抑制病毒增殖和炎症反应来抵抗 RSV 感染。SC的脂质体制剂为提高抗RSV治疗效果提供了一种新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,脂质体槐果碱可能是 RSV 感染的一种有前途的治疗策略,有可能改善婴儿、幼儿和老年人等高危人群的 治疗 结局。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于体内小鼠模型,可能无法完全转化为人类临床结果。证据的强度是中等的,因为该研究在动物模型中证明了有效性,但需要在人体试验中进一步验证。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿、幼儿和老年人严重下呼吸道感染和相关死亡的主要原因。由于 RSV 的高 突变 发生率以及现有 抗病毒药物 药物的疗效和安全性有限,RSV 的临床管理具有挑战性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 RSV 感染的小鼠模型进行体内研究,以评估槐树生物碱及其脂质体制剂的抗 RSV 活性。
analysis_zh.methods: 槐生物碱,特别是槐果碱 (SC),被封装在脂质体中以增强肺滞留和治疗效果。作用机制涉及通过调节 MEK/ERK 信号通路抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化。
analysis_zh.main_results: 体内研究表明,槐花生物碱通过气管内给药可显着降低 RSV 感染小鼠的 死亡率。在小鼠模型中,负载 SC 的脂质体在抑制 RSV 复制和减轻肺部炎症方面优于游离 SC。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究阐明,槐花生物碱通过抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化、抑制病毒增殖和炎症反应来抵抗 RSV 感染。SC的脂质体制剂为提高抗RSV治疗效果提供了一种新方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,脂质体槐果碱可能是 RSV 感染的一种有前途的治疗策略,有可能改善婴儿、幼儿和老年人等高危人群的 治疗 结局。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于体内小鼠模型,可能无法完全转化为人类临床结果。证据的强度是中等的,因为该研究在动物模型中证明了有效性,但需要在人体试验中进一步验证。

papers.title: Large increase in mortality and hospital admissions among young children and the aged due to Influenza and Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Brazil in 2025
papers.abstract: Background: Mortality and hospital admissions due to Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) peaked between January and August 2025 in Brazil. Methods: The Brazilian Ministry of Health data on hospital admissions and deaths caused by SARI were compiled by age group (<5, 5-14, 15-49, 50-64, 65+ years) and quarter between January 2023 and June 2025. SARI causes were aggregated into SARS-Cov-2, Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and other viruses (parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, metapneumovirus). Multinomial regression was used to impute likely causes of death when these were not laboratory confirmed. Results: In the second quarter of 2025 (2025/2), RSV mortality rate among children <5 years reached 60 per 100,000, which is a 43% increase compared with 2024/2. Mortality rate for the joint impact of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus in the same age group doubled from 20 to 40 on the same scale in 2025/2 compared to 2024/2. Over the same period, influenza mortality tripled among the aged, whereas mortality due to other respiratory viruses increased less dramatically, except for SARS-CoV-2, which decreased among the aged from 150 to 25 per 100,000 between 2023/1 and 2025/2. Other age groups remained relatively stable over the period. The variation in hospital admissions largely followed that of mortality. Conclusions: While deaths and hospital admissions caused by SARS-CoV-2 declined rapidly since 2023, mortality rates of other respiratory viruses, mainly influenza and RSV, increased significantly among children <5 years and the aged in 2025/2. Public health policies that facilitate vaccine uptake against these infections should be given high priority.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unexplained surge in severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) mortality and hospital admissions in Brazil during 2025, particularly among young children and older adults, where the role of specific respiratory viruses remained unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compiled Brazilian Ministry of Health data on SARI hospital admissions and deaths by age group (<5, 5-14, 15-49, 50-64, 65+ years) and quarter from January 2023 to June 2025.
analysis.methods: SARI causes were aggregated into SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and other viruses (parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, metapneumovirus). Multinomial regression was used to impute likely causes of death when laboratory confirmation was absent.
analysis.main_results: In the second quarter of 2025, RSV mortality among children under 5 years reached 60 per 100,000, a 43% increase compared with the same period in 2024. Mortality for the combined group of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus doubled from 20 to 40 per 100,000 in the same age group. Influenza mortality tripled among the aged, while SARS-CoV-2 mortality decreased from 150 to 25 per 100,000 in this group between 2023/1 and 2025/2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that while SARS-CoV-2-related mortality declined, mortality due to influenza and RSV increased significantly among children under 5 years and older adults in 2025/2, highlighting a shift in the burden of respiratory viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed Brazilian Ministry of Health data on severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) hospital admissions and deaths from January 2023 to June 2025, stratified by age group and quarter. Using aggregated causes of SARI and multinomial regression for imputation of unconfirmed deaths, the authors observed a marked increase in mortality due to Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) among children under 5 years in the second quarter of 2025, with a 43% rise compared to 2024. Influenza mortality tripled among older adults during the same period, while SARS-CoV-2 mortality declined substantially. The variation in hospital admissions mirrored mortality trends. The authors interpret these findings as a shift in the burden of respiratory viruses, emphasizing the urgent need for enhanced vaccine strategies targeting influenza and RSV in high-risk populations.
