papers.title: Immune correlates of protection against RSV following Ad26.RSV.preF–RSV preF vaccination of adults aged >60 years
papers.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory illness and there is no universally accepted serological correlate of protection (CoP). We evaluated serum pre-fusion immunoglobulin G binding (preF-IgG) and RSV-A2 neutralizing antibodies (RSV-nAb) in adults aged >60 years following vaccination with investigational Ad26.RSV.preF–RSV preF vaccine. PreF-IgG and RSV-nAb measured pre-vaccination (Day 1) and Day 15 post-vaccination were assessed as CoPs against RSV-mediated acute respiratory infection (ARI) and lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD). An increase in both preF-IgG and RSV-nAb at Day 15 was significantly associated with reduced occurrence of RSV-mediated ARI and LRTD during follow-up. Based on controlled vaccine-efficacy curves and Prentice criteria, both markers were identified as CoPs for RSV-mediated ARI and LRTD. These results were validated using samples from a second randomized, phase 3 efficacy trial. Comprehensive profiling of preF-specific antibody responses showed that preF IgG3 and IgG2 may also contribute to protection from RSV.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing of RSV and Phylogeographic Assessment of Viral Importations into Russia
papers.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections caused by the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) pose a major global public health challenge. The use of next-generation sequencing technologies enables detailed monitoring of viral genetic variability, which is crucial for evaluating the efficacy of immunoprophylactic measures. In this study, whole-genome sequencing of RSV was performed on 106 samples collected in the Russian Federation between September 2021 and April 2025. Three NGS platforms were employed: Illumina MiSeq, Oxford Nanopore Technologies MinION, and Qitan Tech QNome-3841. Using discrete phylogeographic methods, we estimated a minimum of 45 introduction events into Russia for RSV-A and 39 for RSV-B among the genomes included in the analysis. Most events were represented by a single Russian genome. These results indicate recurrent introductions of RSV into Russia from abroad. Given the limited genomic sampling available, most of these introductions were not associated with detectable transmission within the country.

The use of next-generation sequencing technologies enables detailed monitoring of viral genetic variability, which is crucial for evaluating the efficacy of immunoprophylactic measures. In this study, whole-genome sequencing of RSV was performed on 106 samples collected in the Russian Federation between September 2021 and April 2025. Three NGS platforms were employed: Illumina MiSeq, Oxford Nanopore Technologies MinION, and Qitan Tech QNome-3841. Using discrete phylogeographic methods, we estimated a minimum of 45 introduction events into Russia for RSV-A and 39 for RSV-B among the genomes included in the analysis. Most events were represented by a single Russian genome. These results indicate recurrent introductions of RSV into Russia from abroad. Given the limited genomic sampling available, most of these introductions were not associated with detectable transmission within the country.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Lower respiratory tract infections caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) represent a major global public health challenge, and the study aimed to address gaps in understanding RSV genetic variability and importation dynamics into Russia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Whole-genome sequencing of RSV was performed on 106 samples collected in the Russian Federation between September 2021 and April 2025, employing discrete phylogeographic methods to assess viral introductions.
analysis.methods: Three next-generation sequencing platforms were used: Illumina MiSeq, Oxford Nanopore Technologies MinION, and Qitan Tech QNome-3841, with whole-genome sequencing applied to characterize RSV genetic diversity.
analysis.main_results: A minimum of 45 introduction events for RSV-A and 39 for RSV-B were estimated, with most events represented by a single Russian genome, indicating recurrent introductions from abroad.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate recurrent RSV introductions into Russia from foreign sources, highlighting the role of genomic surveillance in tracking viral importations and informing public health responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study underscores the value of whole-genome sequencing for monitoring RSV genetic variability and importation patterns, which can guide surveillance strategies and immunoprophylactic measures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The limited genomic sampling restricts detection of transmission chains within Russia, reducing the ability to fully characterize domestic spread and potentially underestimating introduction events.

analysis.summary_en: This study used whole-genome sequencing of 106 RSV samples collected in Russia from 2021 to 2025 to assess viral genetic variability and importation dynamics. Three NGS platforms were employed to sequence RSV genomes, enabling phylogeographic analysis. The authors estimated at least 45 introductions of RSV-A and 39 of RSV-B into Russia, with most events represented by single genomes, suggesting recurrent importations from abroad. These findings highlight the utility of genomic surveillance for tracking RSV introductions and informing public health strategies. However, limited genomic sampling likely constrained detection of domestic transmission chains, limiting the completeness of the phylogeographic assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 引起的下呼吸道感染是一项重大的全球公共卫生挑战,该研究旨在解决了解 RSV 基因变异和俄罗斯输入动态方面的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 2021 年 9 月至 2025 年 4 月期间在俄罗斯联邦收集的 106 个样本进行了 RSV 全 基因组 测序,采用离散系统发育地理学方法来评估病毒引入。
elements_zh.methods: 使用了三个下一代测序平台:Illumina MiSeq、Oxford Nanopore Technologies MinION 和 Qitan Tech QNome-3841,并应用全 基因组 测序来表征 RSV 遗传多样性。
elements_zh.main_results: 据估计,RSV-A 至少有 45 个引入事件,RSV-B 至少有 39 个引入事件,其中大多数事件由单个俄罗斯 基因组 代表,表明来自国外的反复引入。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,RSV 经常从外国来源传入俄罗斯,凸显了 基因组监测 在追踪病毒输入和通报公共卫生应对措施方面的作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调了全 基因组 测序对于监测 RSV 遗传变异和输入模式的价值,它可以指导 监测 策略和免疫预防措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 有限的基因组采样限制了在俄罗斯境内对 传播 链的检测,降低了充分描述国内传播特征的能力,并可能低估了传入事件。

papers.title: Bidirectional changes in recorded pediatric asthma diagnoses with respiratory virus activity: A nationwide interrupted time-series analysis in Japan.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early-life respiratory infections are associated with subsequent asthma development; however, whether respiratory viruses contribute to asthma onset or merely unmask pre-existing susceptibility remains unclear. The COVID-19 pandemic's non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) suppressed respiratory viruses, followed by their resurgence, offering a natural experiment. We examined whether these population-level changes in respiratory virus activity were associated with changes in newly recorded pediatric asthma diagnoses. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide interrupted time-series study using Japan's National Database of Health Insurance Claims, covering approximately 99% of the population. Segmented negative binomial regression with two intervention points-NPI implementation (T1: March 2020) and COVID-19 reclassification (T2: May 2023)-was applied to monthly counts of newly recorded asthma diagnoses among children aged under 19 years (January 2018-March 2024), with atopic dermatitis as negative control. Age-stratified/sex-stratified analyses and exploratory ecological analyses of pathogen-specific associations were conducted. RESULTS: Among 10,508,387 new asthma diagnoses, incidence declined significantly following NPI implementation (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.511, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.422-0.620) and rebounded following NPI relaxation (IRR 1.395, 95% CI:1.120-1.737). Atopic dermatitis showed attenuated changes at both points. Rate differences were greatest in infants (0-1 years) at T1 and school-aged children (5-9 years) at T2. Rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae, but not SARS-CoV-2, correlated with asthma diagnoses in ecological analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Newly recorded pediatric asthma diagnoses showed bidirectional changes that paralleled respiratory virus suppression and resurgence, compatible with a possible contributory role of respiratory infections, particularly among infants and school-aged children.
papers.journal: Allergology international : official journal of the Japanese Society of Allergology

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether respiratory virus activity contributes to pediatric asthma onset or merely unmasks pre-existing susceptibility, noting that early-life respiratory infections are linked to subsequent asthma development but the causal role of specific viruses remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide interrupted time-series study was conducted in Japan using the National Database of Health Insurance Claims, covering approximately 99% of the population, with monthly counts of newly recorded pediatric asthma diagnoses among children under 19 years from January 2018 to March 2024.
analysis.methods: Segmented negative binomial regression with two intervention points—NPI implementation in March 2020 and COVID-19 reclassification in May 2023—was applied to analyze asthma diagnosis trends, including age-stratified and sex-stratified analyses, with atopic dermatitis as a negative control and exploratory ecological analyses of pathogen-specific associations.
analysis.main_results: Among 10,508,387 new asthma diagnoses, incidence declined significantly following NPI implementation (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.511, 95% CI 0.422–0.620) and rebounded after NPI relaxation (IRR 1.395, 95% CI 1.120–1.737), with the greatest rate differences in infants (0–1 years) at T1 and school-aged children (5–9 years) at T2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the bidirectional changes in pediatric asthma diagnoses as compatible with a possible contributory role of respiratory infections, particularly rhinovirus, RSV, influenza, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae, highlighting the novelty of leveraging pandemic-related NPIs as a natural experiment to assess virus-asthma associations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously suggest that respiratory virus activity may influence asthma onset in children, particularly infants and school-aged groups, informing surveillance strategies and future research into infection-mediated asthma triggers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s ecological design and reliance on recorded diagnoses limit causal inference, and the absence of direct pathogen detection in asthma cases weakens specificity; the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide interrupted time-series analysis in Japan examined whether changes in respiratory virus activity during the COVID-19 pandemic were associated with pediatric asthma diagnoses. Using Japan’s National Database of Health Insurance Claims covering 99% of the population, the study analyzed monthly counts of new asthma diagnoses among children under 19 years from January 2018 to March 2024. Segmented negative binomial regression with two intervention points—NPI implementation in March 2020 and COVID-19 reclassification in May 2023—revealed a significant decline in asthma diagnoses following NPIs (IRR 0.511, 95% CI 0.422–0.620) and a rebound after relaxation (IRR 1.395, 95% CI 1.120–1.737). The greatest rate differences were observed in infants at NPI implementation and school-aged children at reclassification. Ecological analyses linked rhinovirus, RSV, influenza, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae to asthma diagnoses, while SARS-CoV-2 showed no correlation. The authors interpret these bidirectional changes as compatible with a contributory role of respiratory infections in asthma onset, particularly among vulnerable age groups. The study’s ecological design and reliance on recorded diagnoses limit causal inference, and the evidence strength is assessed as moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了呼吸道病毒活动是否会导致儿童哮喘发作,还是仅仅揭示了预先存在的易感性,并指出生命早期的呼吸道感染与随后的哮喘发展有关,但特定病毒的因果作用仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 日本利用国家健康保险索赔数据库进行了一项全国性中断时间序列研究,覆盖了约 99% 的人口,每月统计了 2018 年 1 月至 2024 年 3 月期间 19 岁以下儿童新记录的小儿哮喘诊断数量。
elements_zh.methods: 采用具有两个干预点(2020 年 3 月 NPI 实施和 2023 年 5 月 COVID-19 重新分类)的分段负二项回归来分析哮喘 诊断 趋势,包括年龄分层和性别分层分析,以特应性皮炎作为阴性对照,并对病原体特异性关联进行探索性生态分析。
elements_zh.main_results: Among 10,508,387 new asthma diagnoses, incidence declined significantly following NPI implementation (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.511, 95% CI 0.422–0.620) and rebounded after NPI relaxation (IRR 1.395, 95% CI 1.120–1.737), with the greatest rate differences in infants (0–1 years) at T1 and school-aged children (5–9 years) at T2.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将儿科哮喘诊断的双向变化解释为与呼吸道感染(特别是鼻病毒、RSV、流感和肺炎支原体)可能的贡献作用相一致,强调了利用与大流行相关的 NPI 作为评估病毒与哮喘关联的自然实验的新颖性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果谨慎地表明,呼吸道病毒活动可能会影响儿童,特别是婴儿和学龄群体的哮喘发作,为 监测 策略和未来对感染介导的哮喘触发因素的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的生态设计和对记录诊断的依赖限制了因果推断,并且在哮喘病例中缺乏直接病原体检测削弱了特异性;由于这些限制,证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.title_zh: 记录的儿童哮喘诊断与呼吸道病毒活动的双向变化:日本全国范围的中断时间序列分析。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Early-life respiratory infections are associated with subsequent asthma development; however, whether respiratory viruses contribute to asthma onset or merely unmask pre-existing susceptibility remains unclear. The COVID-19 pandemic's non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) suppressed respiratory viruses, followed by their resurgence, offering a natural experiment. We examined whether these population-level changes in respiratory virus activity were associated with changes in newly recorded pediatric asthma diagnoses. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide interrupted time-series study using Japan's National Database of Health Insurance Claims, covering approximately 99% of the population. Segmented negative binomial regression with two intervention points-NPI implementation (T1: March 2020) and COVID-19 reclassification (T2: May 2023)-was applied to monthly counts of newly recorded asthma diagnoses among children aged under 19 years (January 2018-March 2024), with atopic dermatitis as negative control. Age-stratified/sex-stratified analyses and exploratory ecological analyses of pathogen-specific associations were conducted. RESULTS: Among 10,508,387 new asthma diagnoses, incidence declined significantly following NPI implementation (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.511, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.422-0.620) and rebounded following NPI relaxation (IRR 1.395, 95% CI:1.120-1.737). Atopic dermatitis showed attenuated changes at both points. Rate differences were greatest in infants (0-1 years) at T1 and school-aged children (5-9 years) at T2. Rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae, but not SARS-CoV-2, correlated with asthma diagnoses in ecological analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Newly recorded pediatric asthma diagnoses showed bidirectional changes that paralleled respiratory virus suppression and resurgence, compatible with a possible contributory role of respiratory infections, particularly among infants and school-aged children.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了呼吸道病毒活动是否会导致儿童哮喘发作,还是仅仅揭示了预先存在的易感性,并指出生命早期的呼吸道感染与随后的哮喘发展有关,但特定病毒的因果作用仍不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 日本利用国家健康保险索赔数据库进行了一项全国性中断时间序列研究,覆盖了约 99% 的人口,每月统计了 2018 年 1 月至 2024 年 3 月期间 19 岁以下儿童新记录的小儿哮喘诊断数量。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用具有两个干预点(2020 年 3 月 NPI 实施和 2023 年 5 月 COVID-19 重新分类)的分段负二项回归来分析哮喘 诊断 趋势,包括年龄分层和性别分层分析,以特应性皮炎作为阴性对照,并对病原体特异性关联进行探索性生态分析。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将儿科哮喘诊断的双向变化解释为与呼吸道感染(特别是鼻病毒、RSV、流感和肺炎支原体)可能的贡献作用相一致,强调了利用与大流行相关的 NPI 作为评估病毒与哮喘关联的自然实验的新颖性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果谨慎地表明,呼吸道病毒活动可能会影响儿童,特别是婴儿和学龄群体的哮喘发作,为 监测 策略和未来对感染介导的哮喘触发因素的研究提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的生态设计和对记录诊断的依赖限制了因果推断,并且在哮喘病例中缺乏直接病原体检测削弱了特异性;由于这些限制,证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.title: Safety Profile of the Bivalent RSVpreF Vaccine (Abrysvo®) Administered During Pregnancy: An Active Real-World Pharmacovigilance Study in Panama, 2025
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of acute lower respiratory infection in infants. Panama introduced the bivalent prefusion F vaccine (RSVpreF) for administration between 32.0 and 36.6 weeks of gestation in July 2025. In this tropical setting, respiratory viruses are detected throughout the year, with RSV activity increasing during the rainy season. We characterized self-reported maternal and neonatal events and outcomes to generate early post-introduction real-world safety evidence from Central America. This retrospective descriptive observational study included women aged 18 years or older vaccinated with RSVpreF between 32.0 and 36.6 weeks of gestation from July through December 2025 and recruited from January through July 2026. Structured telephone, virtual, or in-person interviews were used. We calculated absolute and relative frequencies and 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Of 225 questionnaires obtained, 200 were eligible for analysis. Mean maternal age was 28.1 years (SD 6.4). At least one reaction was reported by 55.5% of participants, mainly local; injection-site pain was most frequent (48.0%). At least one obstetric condition was reported by 17.5%, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (12.0%). Preterm birth occurred in 2.0% and low birth weight in 2.5%. No fetal or neonatal deaths, thrombocytopenia, paralysis, facial paralysis, or Guillain–Barré syndrome were reported. Jaundice was the most frequent neonatal morbidity (20.0%). In this cohort, self-reported reactogenicity was mainly local, and no unexpected cluster of events was apparent. Participant selection, retrospective self-report, absence of an unvaccinated comparator, and sample size limit risk estimation and detection of uncommon events. The findings provide early active-pharmacovigilance evidence from Central America and support continued surveillance with clinically verified maternal and neonatal outcomes.

It characterized self-reported maternal and neonatal events among 200 vaccinated women aged 18 years or older who received the vaccine between 32.0 and 36.6 weeks of gestation from July to December 2025. Structured interviews were used to collect data, and frequencies with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Reactogenicity was mainly local, with 55.5% reporting at least one reaction and injection-site pain in 48.0%. Obstetric conditions occurred in 17.5%, including hypertensive disorders in 12.0%. papers.title: Etiological composition and epidemiological characteristics of acute respiratory infections in Hebei Province, 2023–2025
papers.abstract: Background Acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) are a major global public health concern. This study aimed to characterize the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological features of 11 common respiratory pathogens among outpatients and hospitalized patients in Hebei Province. Methods A total of 11,942 patients with influenza-like illness (ILI) or severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) were enrolled from October 2023 to September 2025. Throat swabs, sputum, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were collected and screened using a multiplex PCR kit. Age distribution, temporal trends, and coinfection patterns were analyzed. Results The results showed that the pathogen positivity rate among SARI (45.71%) was higher than that among ILI (41.62%); influenza virus (IFV) had the highest detection rate among ILI, whilst Mycoplasma pneumoniae (M. pneumoniae) was the most frequently detected pathogen among SARI; In terms of age distribution: IFV had the highest detection rate across all age groups in ILI; in the 0–4-year-old SARI group, respiratory syncytial virus was predominant; in the 5–14-year-old group, the detection rate of M. pneumoniae reached 43.44 %; and in the group aged 15 years and over, IFV and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2) were the predominant pathogens. SARS-CoV-2 were intermittently detected throughout the year, with three waves of epidemic peaks observed. IFV and RSV predominantly emerged during winter and spring, while rhinovirus showed higher activity in summer and autumn. pneumoniae exhibited a high incidence rate initially, which has been declining steadily since the end of 2024.The proportion of multi-pathogen co-infections among positive specimens was 14.88%, the proportion of co-infections among SARI (23.76 %) was significantly higher than that among ILI (9.28 %). pneumoniae and rhinovirus was the most common, followed by human bocavirus, parainfluenza virus and enterovirus, which were also among the pathogens frequently detected in combination. Conclusion This study elucidated the epidemiological characteristics of respiratory pathogens in Hebei Province, providing a scientific basis for the precise prevention and control of ARTIs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) impose a major global public health burden, and the etiological composition and epidemiological patterns of common respiratory pathogens in Hebei Province were insufficiently characterized before this study.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective surveillance study enrolled 11,942 outpatients and hospitalized patients with influenza-like illness (ILI) or severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) from October 2023 to September 2025 across Hebei Province.
analysis.methods: Throat swabs, sputum, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were collected and screened using a multiplex PCR kit; age distribution, temporal trends, and coinfection patterns were analyzed.
analysis.main_results: Among SARI cases the pathogen positivity rate was 45.71% versus 41.62% in ILI; respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was predominant in the 0–4-year-old SARI group, and RSV showed predominant winter–spring activity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified RSV as a leading cause of SARI in young children and highlighted its seasonal winter–spring predominance, providing new local evidence to inform targeted prevention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support prioritizing RSV surveillance and prevention in pediatric SARI, particularly in the 0–4-year age group, and can guide local immunization and infection-control policies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on multiplex PCR without confirmatory sequencing limit etiological resolution and causal inference; evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective surveillance study in Hebei Province characterized the pathogen spectrum among 11,942 ILI and SARI patients from October 2023 to September 2025 using multiplex PCR on respiratory specimens. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was identified as the predominant pathogen in the 0–4-year-old severe acute respiratory infection group and exhibited clear winter–spring seasonality. The overall pathogen positivity rate was higher in SARI (45.71%) than in ILI (41.62%). These findings provide local evidence to guide RSV-focused prevention and control measures in young children.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性 监测 研究纳入了 2023 年 10 月至 2025 年 9 月河北省 11,942 名患有流感样疾病 (ILI) 或严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 的门诊和住院患者。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) impose a major global public health burden, and the etiological composition and epidemiological patterns of common respiratory pathogens in Hebei Province were insufficiently characterized before this study.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A prospective surveillance study enrolled 11,942 outpatients and hospitalized patients with influenza-like illness (ILI) or severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) from October 2023 to September 2025 across Hebei Province.
analysis_en.methods: Throat swabs, sputum, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were collected and screened using a multiplex PCR kit; age distribution, temporal trends, and coinfection patterns were analyzed.
analysis_en.main_results: Among SARI cases the pathogen positivity rate was 45.71% versus 41.62% in ILI; respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was predominant in the 0–4-year-old SARI group, and RSV showed predominant winter–spring activity.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified RSV as a leading cause of SARI in young children and highlighted its seasonal winter–spring predominance, providing new local evidence to inform targeted prevention strategies.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support prioritizing RSV surveillance and prevention in pediatric SARI, particularly in the 0–4-year age group, and can guide local immunization and infection-control policies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on multiplex PCR without confirmatory sequencing limit etiological resolution and causal inference; evidence strength is moderate.

papers.source_body_en: Background Acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) are a major global public health concern. This study aimed to characterize the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological features of 11 common respiratory pathogens among outpatients and hospitalized patients in Hebei Province. Methods A total of 11,942 patients with influenza-like illness (ILI) or severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) were enrolled from October 2023 to September 2025. Results The results showed that the pathogen positivity rate among SARI (45.71%) was higher than that among ILI (41.62%); influenza virus (IFV) had the highest detection rate among ILI, whilst Mycoplasma pneumoniae (M. pneumoniae) was the most frequently detected pathogen among SARI; In terms of age distribution: IFV had the highest detection rate across all age groups in ILI; in the 0–4-year-old SARI group, respiratory syncytial virus was predominant; in the 5–14-year-old group, the detection rate of M. pneumoniae reached 43.44 %; and in the group aged 15 years and over, IFV and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2) were the predominant pathogens. SARS-CoV-2 were intermittently detected throughout the year, with three waves of epidemic peaks observed. IFV and RSV predominantly emerged during winter and spring, while rhinovirus showed higher activity in summer and autumn. pneumoniae exhibited a high incidence rate initially, which has been declining steadily since the end of 2024.The proportion of multi-pathogen co-infections among positive specimens was 14.88%, the proportion of co-infections among SARI (23.76 %) was significantly higher than that among ILI (9.28 %). pneumoniae and rhinovirus was the most common, followed by human bocavirus, parainfluenza virus and enterovirus, which were also among the pathogens frequently detected in combination. Conclusion This study elucidated the epidemiological characteristics of respiratory pathogens in Hebei Province, providing a scientific basis for the precise prevention and control of ARTIs.

papers.title: Unreacted RSV Polymerase Structures Expand the Post-Translocation Landscape of the Nucleotide Addition Cycle
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) RNA synthesis relies on RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, a complex composed of the L and P proteins. We recently resolved four major structural states of the RSV nucleotide addition cycle (NAC), establishing a framework for viral RNA elongation. However, reaction-derived complexes are influenced by catalytic efficiency and intermediate occupancy and may incompletely sample the NAC conformational landscape. Here, we report two cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of unreacted RSV polymerase bound to a post-translocation RNA product mimic. One structure closely recapitulates the previously determined reaction-derived post-translocation state, demonstrating that the canonical architecture can be recovered independently of nucleotide incorporation. The second structure reveals an additional post-translocation intermediate that retains the same RNA register and vacant +1 product-binding site while adopting a two-domain L organization. Structural comparisons further identify localized rearrangements near the catalytic center, including changes in the motif A loop and supporting helix. Together, these findings expand the structural landscape of the RSV post-translocation stage and refine the current NAC model. More broadly, our results highlight unreacted state-matched complexes as a complementary approach to reaction-derived structures for capturing more complete structural snapshots of dynamic reaction cycles.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved structural analysis of unreacted RSV polymerase using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to capture post-translocation RNA product mimic-bound states. The research was conducted in a laboratory setting and focused on the RSV polymerase complex.
analysis.methods: The researchers used cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to determine two structures of unreacted RSV polymerase bound to a post-translocation RNA product mimic. Structural comparisons were performed to identify localized rearrangements near the catalytic center.
analysis.main_results: Two cryo-EM structures of unreacted RSV polymerase bound to a post-translocation RNA product mimic were reported. One structure closely recapitulates the previously determined reaction-derived post-translocation state, while the second reveals an additional intermediate with a two-domain L organization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings expand the structural landscape of the RSV post-translocation stage and refine the current NAC model. The study highlights unreacted state-matched complexes as a complementary approach to reaction-derived structures for capturing more complete structural snapshots of dynamic reaction cycles.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the structural dynamics of RSV polymerase, which could inform the development of antiviral strategies targeting RNA synthesis. They also contribute to a better understanding of the viral replication process.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to structural analysis and does not include functional or clinical data. The evidence is based on cryo-EM structures and is considered moderate in strength due to the absence of direct biochemical or biological validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) RNA 合成依赖于 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶,这是一种由 L 和 P 蛋白组成的复合物。该研究旨在扩大对 RSV 核苷酸添加循环 (NAC) 易位后阶段的结构理解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及使用冷冻电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 对未反应的 RSV 聚合酶进行结构分析,以捕获易位后 RNA 产物模拟结合状态。该研究是在实验室环境中进行的,重点是 RSV 聚合酶复合物。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用冷冻电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 确定了与易位后 RNA 产物模拟物结合的未反应 RSV 聚合酶的两种结构。进行结构比较以确定催化中心附近的局部重排。
elements_zh.main_results: 报道了与易位后 RNA 产物模拟物结合的未反应 RSV 聚合酶的两种冷冻电镜结构。一种结构紧密地概括了先前确定的反应衍生的易位后状态,而第二种结构则揭示了具有双结构域 L 组织的附加中间体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现扩展了 RSV 易位后阶段的结构景观并完善了当前的 NAC 模型。该研究强调未反应的状态匹配复合物作为反应衍生结构的补充方法,用于捕获动态反应循环的更完整的结构快照。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 RSV 聚合酶结构动力学的深入了解,这可以为针对 RNA 合成的 抗病毒药物 策略的开发提供信息。它们还有助于更好地了解病毒复制过程。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于结构分析,不包括功能或临床数据。该证据基于冷冻电镜结构,由于缺乏直接的生化或生物学验证,因此被认为强度中等。

papers.title: Tidal-Breathing Analysis: A Potential Non-Invasive, Bedside Method for Objective Assessment of Respiratory Mechanics and Bronchodilator Responsiveness in Acute Bronchiolitis—Case Report and Review of the Literature
papers.abstract: Background: Acute bronchiolitis is among the most common causes of lower-respiratory-tract infection in infancy and remains a clinically heterogeneous syndrome. Current international guidelines recommend supportive management and generally discourage routine bronchodilator administration; however, a subset of patients may be physiologically responsive. Tidal-breathing analysis (TBA) is a non-invasive, bedside method for objectively assessing respiratory mechanics and may objectively quantify physiological changes following bronchodilator administration in older children. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 23-month-old boy presenting with a severe RSV bronchiolitis-like wheezing illness complicated by acute respiratory failure. Bronchodilator responsiveness was evaluated using predefined TBA parameters before and after administration of an inhaled bronchodilator. Following treatment, the patient’s time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF) increased from 0.17 to 0.33 s (+94%), while his tPTEF/TE ratio increased from 0.12 to 0.27 (+125%). Expiratory time (TE) and total respiratory cycle duration (Ttot) decreased by 12.6% and 5.1%, respectively, whereas tidal volume (VT) and minute ventilation (MV) increased by 12.1% and 18.3%. Peak expiratory flow remained unchanged (0.14 L/s before and after bronchodilator administration). Discussion: To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first reports of using bedside TBA to characterize acute bronchodilator responsiveness in a severe bronchiolitis-like illness. The improvement in expiratory timing indices, along with the shorter expiratory time without changes in peak expiratory flow, is consistent with improved expiratory flow dynamics following bronchodilator administration. These findings could support the hypothesis that a bronchodilator-responsive physiological phenotype may exist. Previous studies have demonstrated an association between severe bronchiolitis during infancy and subsequent recurrent wheezing or asthma; however, whether acute bronchodilator responsiveness, measured objectively via TBA, is an indication of this phenotype represents a testable hypothesis for future longitudinal studies. Conclusions: This case illustrates the feasibility of bedside TBA for identifying physiological bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis-like illness. Prospective longitudinal studies should be conducted to determine whether TBA-defined responsiveness represents an early physiological marker requiring prospective validation and whether such physiological stratification may support individualized follow-up strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infants, focusing on the central question of whether tidal-breathing analysis (TBA) can objectively assess respiratory mechanics and bronchodilator responsiveness in acute bronchiolitis-like illness caused by RSV.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a case report and narrative synthesis without a systematic search or meta-analysis; it describes a single patient with severe RSV bronchiolitis-like illness and evaluates bronchodilator responsiveness using predefined TBA parameters before and after inhaled bronchodilator administration.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that TBA is feasible for identifying physiological bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis-like illness, with observed increases in time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF) and tPTEF/TE ratio, alongside decreases in expiratory time and total respiratory cycle duration, and increases in tidal volume and minute ventilation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights uncertainty regarding whether TBA-defined bronchodilator responsiveness represents an early physiological marker of subsequent recurrent wheezing or asthma, noting that this hypothesis requires prospective validation in longitudinal studies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that prospective longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether TBA-defined responsiveness can support individualized follow-up strategies and early identification of at-risk infants.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of tidal-breathing analysis (TBA) as a non-invasive bedside method to assess respiratory mechanics and bronchodilator responsiveness in infants with severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis-like illness. A single case report demonstrates that TBA parameters, including time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF) and expiratory timing indices, improved following bronchodilator administration, suggesting a potential bronchodilator-responsive phenotype. However, the review emphasizes that these findings are preliminary and require validation in larger, prospective studies to determine whether TBA-defined responsiveness can predict long-term outcomes such as recurrent wheezing or asthma.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:急性 毛细支气管炎 是婴儿下呼吸道感染的最常见原因之一,并且仍然是一种临床异质综合征。目前的国际指南建议支持性治疗,通常不鼓励常规使用支气管扩张剂;然而,一部分患者可能有生理反应。潮汐呼吸分析 (TBA) 是一种非侵入性床边方法,用于客观评估呼吸力学,并且可以客观量化年龄较大儿童服用支气管扩张剂后的生理变化。病例介绍:我们报告了一名 23 个月大男孩的病例,该男孩患有严重的 RSV 毛细支气管炎 样喘息疾病,并发急性呼吸衰竭。在吸入支气管扩张剂给药前后,使用预定义的 TBA 参数评估支气管扩张剂反应性。治疗 后,患者达到潮气呼气流量峰值的时间 (tPTEF) 从 0.17 秒增加到 0.33 秒 (+94%),而他的 tPTEF/TE 比率从 0.12 增加到 0.27 (+125%)。呼气时间 (TE) 和总呼吸周期持续时间 (Ttot) 分别减少 12.6% 和 5.1%,而潮气量 (VT) 和每分钟通气量 (MV) 增加 12.1% 和 18.3%。呼气峰流量保持不变(支气管扩张剂给药前后均为 0.14 L/s)。讨论:据我们所知,这是使用床边 TBA 来表征严重 毛细支气管炎 类疾病的急性支气管扩张剂反应性的首批报告之一。呼气正时指数的改善,以及呼气峰值流量不变的情况下呼气时间的缩短,与支气管扩张剂给药后呼气流量动力学的改善一致。这些发现可以支持可能存在支气管扩张剂反应性生理表型的假设。先前的研究已证明婴儿期严重的 毛细支气管炎 与随后的复发性喘息或哮喘之间存在关联;然而,通过 TBA 客观测量的急性支气管扩张剂反应性是否表明这种表型代表了未来纵向研究的可检验假设。结论:该病例说明了床边 TBA 确定严重 毛细支气管炎 样疾病中生理性支气管扩张剂反应性的可行性。应进行前瞻性纵向研究,以确定 TBA 定义的反应性是否代表需要前瞻性验证的早期生理标志,以及这种生理分层是否可以支持个体化随访策略。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了婴儿中的人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 毛细支气管炎,重点关注潮汐呼吸分析 (TBA) 是否可以客观评估 RSV 引起的急性 毛细支气管炎 样疾病的呼吸力学和支气管扩张剂反应性的核心问题。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是 病例报告 和叙事综合,没有进行系统搜索或荟萃分析;它描述了一名患有严重 RSV 毛细支气管炎 样疾病的患者,并在吸入支气管扩张剂给药前后使用预定义的 TBA 参数评估支气管扩张剂反应性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,TBA 可用于识别严重 毛细支气管炎 类疾病中的生理支气管扩张剂反应,观察到潮气呼气流量峰值时间 (tPTEF) 和 tPTEF/TE 比值增加,同时呼气时间和总呼吸周期持续时间减少,潮气量和每分钟通气量增加。

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,需要进行前瞻性纵向研究来确定 TBA 定义的反应性是否可以支持个体化随访策略和早期识别高危婴儿。

papers.title: Epidemiology, temporal trends and co-infection of 13 respiratory pathogens in 32,125 children: a 3-year retrospective study
papers.abstract: Background Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections bring heavy global disease burden. Clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features guides clinical management and public health prevention. Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients under 18 years receiving 13-pathogen multiplex PCR at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025. We extracted laboratory data and calculated pathogen positivity, single/co-infection proportions. Stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex and statistical collation of co-infection patterns were completed. Results In total, 32,125 children were included. The total pathogen positive rate reached 63.4%, including 49.8% single infection and 13.6% co-infection dominated by dual infection. Human rhinovirus (22.9%) ranked first, followed by respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%). Pathogens varied obviously across seasons and ages: HRV surged in spring and autumn; parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus prevailed in summer; syncytial virus and influenza peaked in winter. Respiratory syncytial virus mainly affected infants; rhinovirus and parainfluenza were prevalent in toddlers and preschoolers; Mycoplasma pneumoniae rose with age and peaked among school-age children. Dual infection occupied nearly all co-infections; the top non-influenza combinations were HRSV–HRV and HRV–HAdV. Infections with three or more pathogens were rare. Conclusions HRV and HRSV dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with obvious seasonal and age clustering. Most co-infections occurred in winter and young kids. HRV detection requires careful explanation for potential asymptomatic carriage. Local epidemiological characteristics should inform age-and seasonal-targeted diagnosis and targeted prevention including HRSV prevention.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections impose a substantial global disease burden, and clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features is needed to guide clinical management and public health prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study enrolled 32,125 patients under 18 years who underwent 13-pathogen multiplex PCR testing at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025.
analysis.methods: Laboratory data were extracted and analyzed to calculate pathogen positivity, single and co-infection proportions, with stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex.
analysis.main_results: The total pathogen positive rate was 63.4%, including 49.8% single infections and 13.6% co-infections, with dual infections comprising nearly all co-infections; human rhinovirus (22.9%) and respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%) were the most prevalent pathogens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that human rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with clear seasonal and age-related clustering, highlighting the need for careful interpretation of rhinovirus detection due to potential asymptomatic carriage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Local epidemiological patterns should inform age- and season-targeted diagnosis and prevention strategies, including targeted respiratory syncytial virus prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on multiplex PCR results, which may not distinguish asymptomatic carriage from active infection, reducing the certainty of causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed 32,125 children tested for 13 respiratory pathogens at a single Chinese hospital from 2023 to 2025. Overall, 63.4% were positive for at least one pathogen, with human rhinovirus (22.9%) and respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%) most common. Single infections accounted for 49.8% and co-infections for 13.6%, predominantly dual infections. Seasonal and age patterns were evident: rhinovirus peaked in spring and autumn, parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus in summer, and respiratory syncytial virus and influenza in winter. Respiratory syncytial virus primarily affected infants, while rhinovirus and parainfluenza were more prevalent in toddlers and preschoolers. The authors emphasize that local epidemiology should guide targeted diagnosis and prevention, including respiratory syncytial virus prevention, and caution that rhinovirus detection may reflect asymptomatic carriage.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 小儿急性呼吸道感染给全球带来了巨大的疾病负担,需要明确大流行后的流行病学特征来指导临床管理和公共卫生预防。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究纳入了 2023 年至 2025 年在华西第二大学医院接受 13 种病原体多重 PCR 检测的 32,125 名 18 岁以下患者。
elements_zh.methods: 提取并分析实验室数据,计算病原体阳性率、单一感染和合并感染比例,并按年份、季节、年龄和性别进行分层分析。

papers.title_zh: 流行病学,32,125 名儿童中 13 种呼吸道病原体的时间趋势和合并感染:一项为期 3 年的回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Background Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections bring heavy global disease burden. Clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features guides clinical management and public health prevention. Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients under 18 years receiving 13-pathogen multiplex PCR at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025. We extracted laboratory data and calculated pathogen positivity, single/co-infection proportions. Stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex and statistical collation of co-infection patterns were completed. Results In total, 32,125 children were included. The total pathogen positive rate reached 63.4%, including 49.8% single infection and 13.6% co-infection dominated by dual infection. Human rhinovirus (22.9%) ranked first, followed by respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%). Pathogens varied obviously across seasons and ages: HRV surged in spring and autumn; parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus prevailed in summer; syncytial virus and influenza peaked in winter. Respiratory syncytial virus mainly affected infants; rhinovirus and parainfluenza were prevalent in toddlers and preschoolers; Mycoplasma pneumoniae rose with age and peaked among school-age children. Dual infection occupied nearly all co-infections; the top non-influenza combinations were HRSV–HRV and HRV–HAdV. Infections with three or more pathogens were rare. Conclusions HRV and HRSV dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with obvious seasonal and age clustering. Most co-infections occurred in winter and young kids. HRV detection requires careful explanation for potential asymptomatic carriage. Local epidemiological characteristics should inform age-and seasonal-targeted diagnosis and targeted prevention including HRSV prevention.

papers.title: Late preterm and small for gestational age – double the risk?
papers.abstract: Late preterm infants born after 34 + 0 and before 37 + 0 weeks of gestation account for more than 75% of all preterm births so any problems they may have represent a sizeable healthcare burden. It is increasingly recognised that they can suffer greater acute and chronic respiratory morbidity than infants born at term. In a single centre study of 1022 infants, the need for respiratory support was 32%,18% and 11% in infants born at 34, 35 and 36 weeks of gestational age respectively and for supplemental tube feeding was 55%, 24% and 8% respectively. 1 Amongst 1,650,450 infants born between 35 and 41 weeks of gestation between 1998 and 2016, the risks for respiratory, severe neonatal, infectious and neurological morbidities were highest at 35 weeks and gradually decreased until 39 weeks. 2 The results are influenced by ethnicity. In our single centre study Black late preterm infants less frequently needed invasive and non-invasive ventilation and had a shorter duration of length of stay (LOS). 3 Late preterm infants have a higher rate of readmission. 4 They have an increased risk of RSV infection and asthma at 18months and more wheeze and nocturnal cough at school age. 5 In a national cohort of 4,079,878 singletons born in Sweden between 1973 and 2013-4, of whom 14.9% were diagnosed with asthma, the late preterm individuals had 1.31 increased risk of asthma. 6 They also may have poorer lung function at follow-up, 7 particularly if exposed to passive smoking. At three to seven years those born late preterm had worse forced oscillometry results indicating increased peripheral airways resistance, particularly if they had been hospitalised for pulmonary infection and had passive smoke exposure.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the healthcare burden and morbidity associated with late preterm infants, who constitute over 75% of preterm births and face higher risks of respiratory complications compared to term infants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research synthesizes data from multiple cohorts, including a national cohort of 1,650,450 infants born between 35 and 41 weeks of gestation from 1998 to 2016, and a Swedish cohort of 4,079,878 singletons born between 1973 and 2013-4.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed morbidity risks across gestational ages using population-level datasets, with outcomes stratified by gestational week and adjusted for factors such as ethnicity.
analysis.main_results: Risks for respiratory, severe neonatal, infectious, and neurological morbidities were highest at 35 weeks of gestation and gradually decreased until 39 weeks. Late preterm infants had a 1.31 increased risk of asthma compared to term infants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that late preterm birth is associated with elevated risks of respiratory and neurological morbidities, including asthma, with the highest burden observed at 35 weeks of gestation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the need for targeted surveillance and preventive strategies for late preterm infants, particularly those born at 35 weeks, to mitigate long-term respiratory and neurological complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by single-centre data for some analyses and potential confounding by ethnicity and passive smoke exposure, warranting cautious interpretation of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the morbidity risks associated with late preterm birth, defined as delivery between 34 + 0 and 37 + 0 weeks of gestation. Using population-level data from over 1.65 million infants born between 1998 and 2016, the authors report that risks for respiratory, severe neonatal, infectious, and neurological morbidities are highest at 35 weeks of gestation and decline with advancing gestational age. In a Swedish cohort of nearly 4.1 million singletons, late preterm infants exhibited a 1.31-fold increased risk of asthma compared to term infants. The findings emphasize the substantial healthcare burden of late preterm birth and highlight the need for targeted interventions to address respiratory and neurological complications in this vulnerable population.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究综合了多个 队列研究 的数据,其中包括 1998 年至 2016 年期间出生的 1,650,450 名妊娠 35 至 41 周之间出生的婴儿的全国 队列研究,以及 1973 年至 2013-4 年间出生的 4,079,878 名瑞典 队列研究 的数据。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用人口水平数据集分析了不同孕龄的发病风险,结果按孕周分层,并根据种族等因素进行调整。
elements_zh.main_results: 呼吸道疾病、严重新生儿疾病、感染性疾病和神经系统疾病的风险在妊娠 35 周时最高,并逐渐下降,直至 39 周。与足月儿相比,晚期早产儿患哮喘的风险增加 1.31。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,晚期早产与呼吸系统和神经系统疾病(包括哮喘)风险升高相关,其中在妊娠 35 周时观察到的负担最高。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调,晚期早产儿(特别是 35 周出生的早产儿)需要有针对性的 监测 和预防策略,以减轻长期呼吸和神经并发症。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 一些分析的证据受到单中心数据的限制,以及种族和被动吸烟暴露的潜在混淆,需要对研究结果进行谨慎解释。

papers.title: Five-year surveillance of pediatric respiratory pathogens in Fuzhou (2019–2024): impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the epidemiological characteristics and distribution patterns of respiratory pathogens in children in Fuzhou between 2019 and 2024, with a particular focus on changes associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective study included children aged 0–18 years hospitalized for acute respiratory infections in Fuzhou Children’s Hospital of Fujian Province between June 2019 and May 2024. Nasal swab specimens were collected to test for 11 respiratory pathogens using multiplex PCR. The distribution characteristics of pathogens were analyzed across age groups, genders, seasons, and pandemic phases. A total of 37,724 nasal swab specimens were included, comprising 22,327 males and 15,397 females. The overall test positivity rate was 58.78%. Rhinovirus had the highest positivity rate (20.95%), followed by respiratory syncytial virus (11.12%) and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (6.89%). Co-infections were identified in 8.08% of specimens. Multivariable logistic regression revealed distinct age, sex, and seasonal patterns for the three most common pathogens: M. pneumoniae risk increased progressively with age (≥ 6 years: OR = 6.100), RSV predominated in infants, and rhinovirus showed a less pronounced age pattern. Across four pandemic phases (pre-pandemic, strict NPIs, transition, and post-restriction), pathogen detection exhibited distinct trajectories. pneumoniae dropped sharply during the pandemic period and resurged post-restriction (from 1.11% to 12.61%); rhinovirus declined during strict NPIs but rebounded quickly and remained stable; RSV paradoxically increased during strict NPIs (from 10.66% to 26.74%). This study provides evidence on pediatric respiratory pathogen epidemiology in Fuzhou, revealing pathogen-specific changes in detection patterns across different pandemic phases. These findings underscore the importance of continued surveillance and pathogen-targeted prevention strategies in the post-pandemic era.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to understand how the COVID-19 pandemic altered the epidemiology of pediatric respiratory pathogens in Fuzhou, focusing on pathogen-specific changes and gaps in knowledge about their distribution patterns in children.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study enrolled 37,724 children aged 0–18 years hospitalized for acute respiratory infections at Fuzhou Children’s Hospital between June 2019 and May 2024, including 22,327 males and 15,397 females.
analysis.methods: Nasal swab specimens were tested for 11 respiratory pathogens using multiplex PCR, and multivariable logistic regression was applied to analyze age, sex, and seasonal patterns for the most common pathogens.
analysis.main_results: RSV positivity was 11.12% overall, with multivariable analysis showing RSV predominance in infants; RSV detection paradoxically increased during strict non-pharmaceutical interventions (from 10.66% to 26.74%) and declined post-restriction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted RSV’s atypical rise during strict NPIs as a potential consequence of reduced early-life exposure leading to delayed infections, highlighting pathogen-specific pandemic effects not previously detailed in Fuzhou.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted RSV surveillance and prevention strategies in the post-pandemic era, particularly for infants who remain at highest risk during atypical circulation periods.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s single-center retrospective design and reliance on hospital-based sampling limit generalizability to community settings, warranting cautious interpretation of RSV-specific trends.

analysis.summary_en: This five-year retrospective study in Fuzhou analyzed 37,724 pediatric respiratory specimens using multiplex PCR to assess changes in pathogen detection across pandemic phases. RSV was detected in 11.12% of cases, with multivariable analysis confirming its predominance in infants. Notably, RSV positivity paradoxically increased during strict non-pharmaceutical interventions (from 10.66% to 26.74%) before declining post-restriction, suggesting pandemic-related shifts in transmission dynamics. Rhinovirus remained the most frequently detected pathogen overall. The authors propose that reduced early-life exposure during NPIs may have delayed RSV infections, underscoring the need for continued surveillance and targeted prevention in the post-pandemic period. However, as a single-center study, findings may not reflect community-level trends.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究纳入了 2019 年 6 月至 2024 年 5 月期间在福州儿童医院因急性呼吸道感染住院的 37,724 名 0-18 岁儿童,其中男性 22,327 名,女性 15,397 名。

papers.abstract_zh: 本研究旨在调查2019年至2024年福州市儿童呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征和分布模式,特别关注与COVID-19大流行相关的变化。这项回顾性研究纳入了2019年6月至2024年5月期间在福建省福州儿童医院因急性呼吸道感染住院的0-18岁儿童。收集鼻拭子标本,采用多重PCR检测11种呼吸道病原体。分析病原体在年龄组、性别、季节和流行阶段的分布特征。共纳入37,724份鼻拭子样本,其中男性22,327人,女性15,397人。总体检测阳性率为58.78%。鼻病毒阳性率最高(20.95%),其次是呼吸道合胞病毒(11.12%)和肺炎支原体(6.89%)。8.08% 的标本中发现了双重感染。多变量逻辑回归揭示了三种最常见病原体的不同年龄、性别和季节模式:肺炎支原体风险随着年龄的增长而逐渐增加(≥ 6 岁:OR = 6.100),RSV 在婴儿中占主导地位,而鼻病毒则表现出不太明显的年龄模式。在四个大流行阶段(大流行前、严格的 NPI、过渡和限制后),病原体检测表现出不同的轨迹。肺炎疫情期间大幅下降,限购后回升(从1.11%上升至12.61%);鼻病毒在严格的 NPI 期间有所下降,但迅速反弹并保持稳定;在严格的 NPI 期间,RSV 反而增加(从 10.66% 增加到 26.74%)。这项研究提供了福州儿童呼吸道病原体 流行病学 的证据,揭示了不同流行阶段检测模式的病原体特异性变化。这些发现强调了大流行后时代持续的 监测 和针对病原体的预防策略的重要性。

papers.title: Bayesian epidemic alignment for causal evaluation of seasonal infectious-disease interventions
papers.abstract: Seasonal infectious-disease interventions are commonly evaluated with interrupted time-series or pre--post designs that align epidemics by calendar week. When epidemic onset, speed or peak timing differs between seasons, such comparisons confound a shift in epidemic phase with a change in disease burden. We propose a Bayesian causal count model in which season-specific affine transformations map calendar time to a latent epidemic clock, and intervention effects are estimated on that clock rather than on the calendar. The alignment is a model component rather than a preprocessing step, so uncertainty about epidemic timing propagates into every causal contrast. The model uses a negative-binomial observation distribution, hierarchical area, season and area-season effects, a shrunk Fourier epidemic curve, and a continuous programme-intensity exposure. Posterior g-computation yields prevented cases, prevented fractions, peak attenuation and epidemic displacement, under both a controlled contrast and a dynamic contrast that propagates disease history within each arm. A two-tier simulation study evaluates bias, root mean squared error, interval coverage and parameter recovery under stable timing, epidemic-clock variation, intensity-dependent ascertainment and area-level confounding. We illustrate the framework using open Catalan primary-care surveillance and respiratory syncytial virus immunisation data, with explicit attention to the overlap in programme intensity that identifies the effect.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a Bayesian causal count model to evaluate seasonal infectious-disease interventions, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The model aligns epidemics using a latent epidemic clock rather than calendar time, allowing uncertainty in timing to propagate into causal contrasts. It uses a negative-binomial distribution and hierarchical effects to estimate intervention impacts, including prevented cases and peak attenuation. The framework is demonstrated using Catalan primary-care surveillance and RSV immunisation data, highlighting the importance of programme intensity overlap in identifying effects. A simulation study assesses the model's performance under various conditions, providing moderate evidence for its validity. The approach offers new insights into causal evaluation by addressing limitations of traditional pre-post designs, which can confound changes in epidemic timing with shifts in disease burden. This could improve surveillance and intervention strategies for RSV, particularly in settings with overlapping programme intensity and epidemic patterns.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 季节性传染病干预措施通常采用中断时间序列或按日历周调整流行病的前后设计进行评估。该研究通过提出贝叶斯因果计数模型来解决这些方法的局限性,该模型可以解释流行时间的不确定性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究提出了贝叶斯因果计数模型来评估季节性传染病干预措施。它使用开放的加泰罗尼亚初级保健 监测 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 免疫数据来说明该框架。
elements_zh.methods: 该模型使用负二项式观测分布、分层区域、季节和区域-季节效应、收缩的傅立叶流行曲线和连续的程序强度暴露。在受控对比度和传播每只手臂内疾病史的动态对比度下,后 g 计算可预防病例、预防分数、峰值衰减和流行性位移。
elements_zh.main_results: 对齐是一个模型组件而不是预处理步骤,因此流行时间的不确定性会传播到每个因果对比中。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该模型通过将流行时间的不确定性直接纳入分析框架,为季节性传染病干预措施的因果评估提供了一种新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架可以为设计更准确的 监测 系统和 呼吸道合胞病毒 干预措施提供信息,特别是在计划强度与流行病时间重叠的情况下。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 两层模拟研究评估稳定时间、流行病时钟变化、强度相关确定和区域级混杂下的偏差、均方根误差、区间覆盖和参数恢复。由于该研究基于模拟和仅抽象数据,因此证据并不充分。

papers.full_text: The Journal for Translational Respiratory Immunology is a rigorous, peer-reviewed scientific journal dedicated to publishing high-impact research at the critical intersection of the respiratory system and immune defense mechanisms. Our mission is to accelerate the translation of basic scientific discoveries into actionable clinical practice, bridging the gap between laboratory research (bench) and patient care (bedside) to ultimately improve global respiratory health. The journal provides a dynamic and comprehensive platform for researchers, clinicians, and academicians to share novel insights, experimental findings, and clinical trials. We focus on the complex biological mechanisms by which immunological and virological factors influence respiratory health and drive the pathogenesis of pulmonary diseases. The journal is committed to advancing medical science by fostering interdisciplinary collaboration among specialists in respiratory care, virology, and immunopathology. news.content_title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) News, Articles and Research
news.content: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Nirsevimab is a long-acting monoclonal antibody that provides season-long protection against RSV in infants, reducing medically attended infections and hospitalizations. Maternal vaccination and nirsevimab together offer complementary strategies to protect newborns during their highest-risk months. Overview Feature Articles Latest Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) News and Research Early-infancy infection with RSV increases the risk of developing childhood asthma Belgian scientists from VIB and Ghent University (UGent), together with Danish collaborators, have uncovered compelling evidence that early-infancy infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) significantly increases the risk of developing childhood asthma-especially in children with a family history of allergy or asthma. Year-round access to RSV immunization may reduce major seasonal outbreaks Providing year-round access to RSV immunization would minimize the risk of large seasonal outbreaks across the nation, including in both urban and rural areas. Preparing for the respiratory virus season: A guide for families As respiratory virus season begins, pediatric experts are preparing for an expected rise in cases of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), which can cause cold-like symptoms in most people but serious illness in infants and older adults. COVID-19, RSV, and flu vaccines remain safe and effective The systematic review provides crucial insights into the efficacy and safety of respiratory virus vaccines, supporting evidence-based immunization practices. Study reveals impact of viral combinations on infant respiratory illness severity A new study led by researchers at National Jewish Health has revealed that, while a wide range of viruses can cause lower respiratory tract illnesses (LRIs) in infants, certain viruses and viral combinations dramatically increase the risk of severe disease. A parent's guide to manage pediatric respiratory illnesses during the virus season As we head deeper into fall and toward the holiday season, your little one may start to exhibit symptoms like a runny nose, cough, or fever. HEPA purifiers do not fully reduce classroom viral exposure In a secondary analysis of a study of 200 classrooms, Mass General Brigham researchers found respiratory viral exposures were still high in those with HEPA purifiers, suggesting additional interventions are needed. RSV vaccines protect two most-at-risk groups from severe illness The review demonstrates that vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are both safe and effective in protecting groups who are most at risk for serious illness, including older adults and infants. Soap shortages undermine global hand hygiene efforts A lack of soap is the most often reported barrier to effective hand hygiene-key to curbing the spread of infection-in shared community spaces, such as households, schools, and public places, finds a systematic review of the available research, published in the open access journal BMJ Global Health. RSV vaccine slashes hospitalizations in older adults in real-world trial A large, real-world randomized trial in Denmark found that the RSVpreF vaccine reduced RSV-related hospitalizations in adults aged 60 and over by over 80%. The vaccine also showed protection against broader respiratory illness with a favorable safety profile. Healthy newborns also face high risk of severe RSV infection It is not only premature babies and children with underlying diseases who suffer from serious respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections. Can an allergy spray help prevent COVID-19? Researchers determine the efficacy and safety of azelastine nasal spray for preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection in healthy adults. How effective is the RSV vaccine for older adults? A single dose of the RSV vaccine offers 58% protection against hospitalization in older adults, but effectiveness varies in immunocompromised individuals. New guidelines improve care for respiratory infections in leukemia patients People with leukemia have a weakened immune system due to the disease itself and treatment, which leads to an increased susceptibility to infections. RSV causes severe outcomes and heart complications in older adults Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a well-known cause of infections in children, but it's understudied in older individuals. Maternal RSV vaccination linked to sharp drop in infant lung infections Vaccination of pregnant women has been linked to a drop in newborns being admitted to hospital with a serious lung infection, research suggests. Light-activated drug discovery identifies broad-spectrum antivirals UC Santa Barbara researchers and collaborators from campus biotech spinoff Integrated Biosciences, as well as Harvard, MIT and genomics company Illumina Ventures are using optogenetics - the use of light to probe the functions of living tissue - to find compounds to help our bodies more effectively help themselves in times of physiological stress. How underreporting masks the real impact of RSV in older populations Research shows RSV leads to high hospitalization rates in adults, emphasizing the importance of enhanced surveillance and diagnostic measures in healthcare. New RSV guideline aims to standardize pediatric care across China Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections (ALRTIs) in children under five and poses a persistent threat to child health worldwide. WHO releases first-ever position paper on immunization products to protect infants against RSV Today, the World Health Organization (WHO) published its first-ever position paper on immunization products to protect infants against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) – the leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections in children globally

dependency hospital units with RSV chest infection in winter 2025/2026, down from 131 the year prior. The maternal RSV programme started in September 2024 REC Stock Footage / Shutterstock.com The number of infants admitted to intensive care with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) reduced by half after the first full year of the maternal RSV vaccination programme, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA)’s RSV annual report, published on 13 August 2026. Across the 20 NHS trusts taking part in the UKHSA surveillance, there were 63 infants under 6 months age admitted to intensive care units (ICU) or higher dependency units (HDU) with confirmed RSV chest infection in the winter season 2025/2026. The previous year, the same 20 trusts reported 131 infants aged under 6 months were admitted to ICU or HDU, the UKHSA said. “This demonstrates the strong impact that the first full year of the maternal programme has had in protecting newborns from severe RSV disease,” it added. While the maternal RSV programme started in September 2024, its full impact on reducing the number of cases and severity of RSV in infants was not expected to be seen until the winter of 2025/2026, as more pregnant women became eligible over the course of the past year, UKHSA said. Ashifa Trivedi, neonatal pharmacist and clinical lead at Evelina London Children’s Hospital, said the results were “really encouraging to see”. “For those of us working in paediatrics, we know just how unwell young babies with RSV can become, and the impact this has on babies, families and paediatric services. This data shows [sic] what effective prevention can achieve,” she said. Stephen Tomlin, clinical lead for the neonatal and paediatric pharmacy group (NPPG), said: “A 50% reduction in ICU and HDU admissions among infants under six months is a significant achievement and demonstrates the value of protecting babies before they are born. “Preventing babies from requiring intensive care is one of the clearest measures of success for any vaccination programme, and these findings suggest that maternal immunisation is already delivering substantial benefits for families and the NHS.” The report also revealed that 61.7% of women giving birth had received an RSV vaccine between March 2025 and February 2026. Trivedi commented: “There is still more we can do to ensure every eligible woman has the opportunity to make an informed choice about vaccination and that access is equitable across all communities. As healthcare professionals we have an important role in supporting conversations with families, providing clear and trusted information, and helping to address barriers to vaccination so that more babies can benefit from this protection.” Tomlin added: “While uptake exceeds 60%, thousands of infants remain unprotected each year. Every contact that healthcare professionals have with pregnant women is an opportunity to discuss the importance of RSV vaccination and its role in safeguarding newborns during their most vulnerable months of life... Improving awareness of RSV vaccination during pregnancy should remain a priority across maternity, primary care and pharmacy services.” Last updated 13 August 2026 14:03 Citation The Pharmaceutical Journal, PJ August 2026, Vol 321, No 8012;321(8012)::DOI:10.1211/PJ.2026.1.424477 Please leave a comment Cancel reply You must be logged in to post a comment. Across the 20 NHS trusts taking part in the UKHSA surveillance, there were 63 infants under 6 months age admitted to intensive care units (ICU) or higher dependency units (HDU) with confirmed RSV chest infection in the winter season 2025/2026. The previous year, the same 20 trusts reported 131 infants aged under 6 months were admitted to ICU or HDU, the UKHSA said. “This demonstrates the strong impact that the first full year of the maternal programme has had in protecting newborns from severe RSV disease,” it added. While the maternal RSV programme started in September 2024, its full impact on reducing the number of cases and severity of RSV in infants was not expected to be seen until the winter of 2025/2026, as more pregnant women became eligible over the course of the past year, UKHSA said. Ashifa Trivedi, neonatal pharmacist and clinical lead at Evelina London Children’s Hospital, said the results were “really encouraging to see”. “For those of us working in paediatrics, we know just how unwell young babies with RSV can become, and the impact this has on babies, families and paediatric services. This data shows [sic] what effective prevention can achieve,” she said. Stephen Tomlin, clinical lead for the neonatal and paediatric pharmacy group (NPPG), said: “A 50% reduction in ICU and HDU admissions among infants under six months is a significant achievement and demonstrates the value of protecting babies before they are born. “Preventing babies from requiring intensive care is one of the clearest measures of success for any vaccination programme, and these findings suggest that maternal immunisation is already delivering substantial benefits for families and the NHS.” The report also revealed that 61.7% of women giving birth had received an RSV vaccine between March 2025 and February 2026. Trivedi commented: “There is still more we can do to ensure every eligible woman has the opportunity to make an informed choice about vaccination and that access is equitable across all communities. As healthcare professionals we have an important role in supporting conversations with families, providing clear and trusted information, and helping to address barriers to vaccination so that more babies can benefit from this protection.” Tomlin added: “While uptake exceeds 60%, thousands of infants remain unprotected each year. Every contact that healthcare professionals have with pregnant women is an opportunity to discuss the importance of RSV vaccination and its role in safeguarding newborns during their most vulnerable months of life... news.content: Medscape AI News & Perspective Tools & Reference CME/CE More EN RegisterLog In AI Mode Medscape News UK RSV Maternal Vaccine Halves Baby Intensive Care Admissions Rob Hicks, MBBS August 16, 2026 0 Add to Email Alerts Jump to Key Points The NHS maternal vaccine programme for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has “halved” the number of babies needing support in ICUs in its first full year, new figures suggest. The UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) annual report showed the impact of the maternal vaccination programme for the first time. It found that around 50% fewer infants under 6 months had been admitted to intensive care with RSV disease in England. The UKHSA said that as the vaccination programme took fuller effect, there was lower RSV activity. According to the agency, last winter (2025-2026), in the 20 NHS trusts taking part in the surveillance, 63 infants younger than 6 months were admitted to ICU or higher-dependency units with confirmed RSV chest infection. The previous year, 2024-2025, the same 20 trusts reported 131 admissions. Officials said the reduction in admissions “demonstrates the strong impact that the first full year of the maternal programme has had in protecting newborns from severe RSV disease.” SUGGESTED FOR YOU Many Babies Still At Risk The maternal vaccination programme — which began in September 2024 — is offered to women from 28 weeks of pregnancy to protect newborns, who are at higher risk for severe illness from RSV. Earlier this year, a UKHSA study presented at the ESCMID conference showed a dose of the maternal vaccine provided over 80% protection to a newborn infant against hospital admission. However, the UKHSA warned that many thousands of babies were still at risk. In England, in the 12 months from March 2025 to February 2026, 61.7% of women giving birth had received an RSV vaccine. In Wales, in the 12 months from June 2025 to May 2026, this figure was 56.2%. In Scotland, 53.7% of pregnant women who reached 28 weeks of pregnancy had received an RSV vaccine since the start of the programme. Dr Conall Watson, immunisation consultant at the UKHSA, said in a press release that RSV caused a “horrible” chest infection, but is now preventable with a vaccine that he described as highly effective with an excellent safety profile. Infant Bronchiolitis Lower The UKHSA pointed out that whilst there is no risk-free birth month, babies born in late summer or the autumn are most likely to be admitted to hospital from RSV. The UK RSV season usually started in October; however, last winter cases did not start to rise until early November, peaking during late December. They then steadily declined and reached low levels in March 2026. In England in 2025-2026, peak weekly infant A&E attendances for bronchiolitis — where most cases are due to RSV — were lower than in previous seasons, and the peak season was shorter. The report also found that 65% of eligible older adults had received an RSV vaccine by the end of May this year, and that vaccination in England had resulted in a sustained reduction of over 40% in RSV-related hospitalisation rates among eligible adults 75-80 years of age. “Thanks to NHS staff dozens of new-borns have potentially avoided being admitted to intensive care after their mother received her RSV jab during pregnancy,” said Caroline Temmink, NHS director of vaccinations, in a press release. Dr Mike McKean, vice-president for policy at the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, told Medscape UK News that it was “fantastic” to see newborn ICU admissions halved since the introduction of the RSV vaccine. “It shows how vital this vaccine is in protecting newborns from this nasty infection and helping to ease pressure on NHS services,” he said. Rob Hicks is a retired National Health Service doctor. A well-known TV and radio broadcaster, he has written several books and has regularly contributed to national newspapers, magazines, and online publications. He is based in the United Kingdom. 50% in first year of RSV vaccine programme Open Access News Health & Social Care Newborn ICU admissions drop 50% in first year of RSV vaccine programme August 13, 2026 image: ©Hailshadow| iStock Data from the UK Health Security Agency shows that admissions of infants under six months to intensive care for respiratory syncytial virus dropped by 50 per cent during the first full year of the maternal vaccination programme According to the UKHSA annual report, surveillance across 20 NHS trusts recorded 63 infants under six months admitted to intensive care or high dependency units with confirmed RSV chest infections during the 2025–2026 winter season. This represents a 50 per cent decrease from the 131 admissions reported by the same hospital trusts in 2024–2025. The report evaluates the initial impact of the maternal vaccination scheme introduced in September 2024, which offers the vaccine to pregnant women from 28 weeks of pregnancy. Between March 2025 and February 2026, 61.7 per cent of women giving birth had received the vaccine. Maternal antibodies pass through the placenta to provide newborns with immediate protection against severe disease from birth. Reduced A&E demand and altered seasonal trends In addition to reducing intensive care admissions, the maternal vaccine contributed to lower hospital emergency department attendances for bronchiolitis, a common lung infection primarily caused by RSV. Peak weekly A&E attendances for infant bronchiolitis were lower than in previous years, and the peak season was shorter. The overall 2025–2026 RSV season started later than usual, with cases rising in early November, peaking in December, and declining to low levels by March 2026. Prior UKHSA research presented at the ESCMID conference indicates that maternal vaccination provides over 80 per cent protection against hospital admission for newborn infants. Senior adult outcomes and broader impact The annual report also examined the impact of the RSV vaccine rollout among older adults. By the end of May 2026, 65 per cent of eligible adults had received their vaccine. Vaccine impact analysis across England demonstrated a sustained reduction of over 40 per cent in RSV-related hospitalisations among adults aged 75 to 80 years. Health officials advise that pregnant women past 28 weeks contact their maternity services or GP practices to arrange vaccination prior to the autumn virus season. analysis.event: UK Health Security Agency reported a 50% drop in RSV-confirmed ICU admissions among infants under six months during the first full year of a maternal RSV vaccination programme, alongside reduced A&E bronchiolitis attendances and altered seasonal trends.
